	// hasRequiredStatusContexts is true when at least one required status-check context must be satisfied:
	// the branch protection's own contexts and/or required scoped workflow checks.
	// The latter gate the merge even when the rule's own status check is disabled.
	hasRequiredStatusContexts bool

	hasOverridableBlockers     bool
	canMergeNow                bool // PR is mergeable, either no blocker, or doer can bypass the blockers
	hasPermToMerge             bool // doer has permission to merge
	canBypassProtection        bool
	canBypassProtectionAsAdmin bool

	ShowUpdatePullInfo  bool
	UpdatePrimaryAction *pullUpdateAction
	UpdateStyleOptions  []*pullUpdateAction

	MergeFormProps        map[string]any
	ShowPullCommands      bool
	ShowMergeInstructions bool
	AutodetectManualMerge bool

	// don't expose unneeded fields to templates, need more refactoring changes
	hasStatusCheckBlocker bool
	IsPullBranchDeletable bool

	isBlockedByApprovals              bool
	isBlockedByRejection              bool
	isBlockedByOfficialReviewRequests bool
	isBlockedByOutdatedBranch         bool
	isBlockedByChangedProtectedFiles  bool
	requireSigned, willSign           bool
	signingKeyMergeDisplay            string

	infoCommitBlockers     pullMergeBoxInfoItemCollection
	infoProtectionBlockers pullMergeBoxInfoItemCollection
	infoMergePrompts       pullMergeBoxInfoItemCollection

	InfoSections []*pullInfoSection
}

type pullUpdateAction struct {
	URL      string
	Text     template.HTML
	Selected bool
}

// pullRequestViewInfo is a structured type for viewing pull request
// Refactoring plan:
// * move dynamic template-data-based variable into this struct
// * let backend handle complex logic, prepare everything, avoid plenty of "if" blocks in tmpl
type pullRequestViewInfo struct {
	issue *issues_model.Issue

	IsPullRequestBroken bool
	HeadBranchCommitID  string
	headTarget          string // for display purpose only

	CompareInfo         git_service.CompareInfo
	ProtectedBranchRule *git_model.ProtectedBranch
	MergeBoxData        *pullMergeBoxData

	workInProgressPrefix string
}

func newPullRequestViewInfo() *pullRequestViewInfo {
	return &pullRequestViewInfo{}
}

    52	func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) prepareMergeBoxIconColor() {
    53		pull := prInfo.issue.PullRequest
    54		mergeBoxData := prInfo.MergeBoxData
    55	
    56		showAsNormalColor := prInfo.issue.IsClosed || prInfo.workInProgressPrefix != "" || pull.IsEmpty() || pull.IsFilesConflicted()
    57		showAsErrorColor := false
    58		showAsWarningColor := pull.IsChecking()
    59	
    60		if statusCheckData := mergeBoxData.StatusCheckData; statusCheckData != nil {
    61			showAsErrorColor = statusCheckData.pullCommitStatusState.IsError() || statusCheckData.pullCommitStatusState.IsFailure() ||
    62				statusCheckData.RequiredChecksState.IsError() || statusCheckData.RequiredChecksState.IsFailure()
    63	
    64			showAsWarningColor = showAsWarningColor ||
    65				statusCheckData.pullCommitStatusState.IsWarning() || statusCheckData.pullCommitStatusState.IsPending() ||
    66				((mergeBoxData.enableStatusCheck || mergeBoxData.hasRequiredStatusContexts) && (statusCheckData.RequiredChecksState.IsWarning() || statusCheckData.RequiredChecksState.IsPending()))
    67		}
    68	
    69		hasBlockers := len(mergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.items) > 0 || len(mergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.items) > 0
    70	
    71		switch {
    72		case pull.HasMerged:
    73			prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-purple"
    74		case showAsNormalColor:
    75			prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-text-light"
    76		case showAsErrorColor:
    77			prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-red"
    78		case showAsWarningColor:
    79			prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-yellow"
    80		case hasBlockers:
    81			prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-red"
    82		case pull.IsStatusMergeable():
    83			prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-green"
    84		default:
    85			prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-text-light"
    86		}
    87	}

    89	func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) prepareMergeBoxInfoItems(ctx *context.Context) {
    90		pull := prInfo.issue.PullRequest
    91		data := prInfo.MergeBoxData
    92	
    93		if pull.HasMerged && data.IsPullBranchDeletable {
    94			data.ClosedInfoTitle = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.merged_success")
    95			data.ClosedInfoBody = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.merged_info_text", htmlutil.HTMLFormat("<code>%s</code>", prInfo.headTarget))
    96			return
    97		} else if prInfo.issue.IsClosed {
    98			data.ClosedInfoTitle = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.closed")
    99			if prInfo.IsPullRequestBroken {
   100				data.ClosedInfoBody = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.cant_reopen_deleted_branch")
   101			} else {
   102				data.ClosedInfoBody = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.reopen_to_merge")
   103			}
   104			return
   105		}
   106	
   107		if pull.IsFilesConflicted() {
   108			detailItems := escapeStringSliceToHTML(pull.ConflictedFiles)
   109			if len(detailItems) == 0 {
   110				detailItems = append(detailItems, ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.files_conflicted_no_listed_files"))
   111			}
   112			if len(detailItems) > 10 {
   113				detailItems = detailItems[:10]
   114				detailItems = append(detailItems, "...")
   115			}
   116			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
   117				svg.RenderHTML("octicon-x"),
   118				ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.files_conflicted"),
   119				detailItems,
   120			)
   121		}
   122	
   123		if prInfo.IsPullRequestBroken {
   124			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
   125				svg.RenderHTML("octicon-x"),
   126				ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.data_broken"),
   127			)
   128		}
   129	
   130		if pull.IsChecking() {
   131			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
   132				svg.RenderHTML("gitea-running", 16, "rotate-clockwise"),
   133				ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.is_checking"),
   134			)
   135		}
   136	
   137		if pull.IsAncestor() {
   138			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
   139				svg.RenderHTML("octicon-alert"),
   140				ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.is_ancestor"),
   141			)
   142		}
   143	
   144		if !pull.IsStatusMergeable() {
   145			// it is only a "protection" level blocker, it can be bypassed by admin (e.g.: manually merged)
   146			if pull.IsEmpty() {
   147				prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddInfoItem(
   148					svg.RenderHTML("octicon-alert"),
   149					ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.is_empty"),
   150				)
   151			} else {
   152				prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddErrorItem(ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.cannot_auto_merge_desc"))
   153				prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddInfoItem(
   154					svg.RenderHTML("octicon-info"),
   155					ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.cannot_auto_merge_helper"),
   156				)
   157			}
   158		}
   159	
   160		if !data.hasPermToMerge {
   161			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddInfoItem(
   162				svg.RenderHTML("octicon-info"),
   163				ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.no_merge_access"),
   164			)
   165		}
   166	
   167		if data.canMergeNow {
   168			if data.hasOverridableBlockers {
   169				prompt := ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.required_status_check_bypass_allowlist")
   170				if data.canBypassProtectionAsAdmin {
   171					prompt = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.required_status_check_administrator")
   172				}
   173				prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoMergePrompts.AddInfoItem(
   174					svg.RenderHTML("octicon-dot-fill"),
   175					prompt,
   176				)
   177			} else if pull.IsStatusMergeable() || pull.IsEmpty() {
   178				prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoMergePrompts.AddInfoItem(
   179					svg.RenderHTML("octicon-check"),
   180					ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.can_auto_merge_desc"),
   181				)
   182			}
   183		}
   184	
   185		if len(data.infoCommitBlockers.items) > 0 {
   186			data.InfoSections = append(data.InfoSections, &pullInfoSection{data.infoCommitBlockers.items})
   187		} else {
   188			data.InfoSections = append(data.InfoSections, &pullInfoSection{data.infoProtectionBlockers.items})
   189		}
   190		data.InfoSections = append(data.InfoSections, &pullInfoSection{data.infoMergePrompts.items})
   191	}

func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) prepareMergeBox(ctx *context.Context, issue *issues_model.Issue) {
	if prInfo.issue != issue {
		panic("impossible, issue must be the same")
	}

	pull := issue.PullRequest
	data := &pullMergeBoxData{}
	prInfo.MergeBoxData = data

	canDelete := false
	canWriteToHeadRepo := false

	pull_service.StartPullRequestCheckOnView(ctx, pull)

	if !prInfo.IsPullRequestBroken {
		data.ShowUpdatePullInfo = pull.CommitsBehind > 0 && !issue.IsClosed && !pull.IsChecking() && !pull.IsFilesConflicted() && !prInfo.IsPullRequestBroken
		prInfo.preparePullUpdateActions(ctx)
		if ctx.Written() {
			return
		}
	}

	if ctx.IsSigned {
		if err := pull.LoadHeadRepo(ctx); err != nil {
			log.Error("LoadHeadRepo: %v", err)
		} else if pull.HeadRepo != nil {
			perm, err := access_model.GetDoerRepoPermission(ctx, pull.HeadRepo, ctx.Doer)
			if err != nil {
				ctx.ServerError("GetDoerRepoPermission", err)
				return
			}
			if perm.CanWrite(unit.TypeCode) {
				// Check if branch is not protected
				if pull.HeadBranch != pull.HeadRepo.DefaultBranch {
					if protected, err := git_model.IsBranchProtected(ctx, pull.HeadRepo.ID, pull.HeadBranch); err != nil {
						log.Error("IsProtectedBranch: %v", err)
					} else if !protected {
						canDelete = true
						ctx.Data["DeleteBranchLink"] = issue.Link() + "/cleanup"
					}
				}
				canWriteToHeadRepo = true
			}
		}

		if err := pull.LoadBaseRepo(ctx); err != nil {
			log.Error("LoadBaseRepo: %v", err)
		}
		perm, err := access_model.GetDoerRepoPermission(ctx, pull.BaseRepo, ctx.Doer)
		if err != nil {
			ctx.ServerError("GetDoerRepoPermission", err)
			return
		}
		if !canWriteToHeadRepo { // maintainers maybe allowed to push to head repo even if they can't write to it
			canWriteToHeadRepo = pull.AllowMaintainerEdit && perm.CanWrite(unit.TypeCode)
		}
		data.hasPermToMerge, err = pull_service.IsUserAllowedToMerge(ctx, pull, perm, ctx.Doer)
		if err != nil {
			ctx.ServerError("IsUserAllowedToMerge", err)
			return
		}

		if ctx.Data["CanMarkConversation"], err = issues_model.CanMarkConversation(ctx, issue, ctx.Doer); err != nil {
			ctx.ServerError("CanMarkConversation", err)
			return
		}
	}

	data.ShowMergeInstructions = canWriteToHeadRepo
	data.ShowPullCommands = pull.HeadRepo != nil && !pull.HasMerged && !issue.IsClosed

	prInfo.prepareMergeBoxProtectionChecks(ctx)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}

	prInfo.prepareMergeBoxCommitSigning(ctx)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}

	prInfo.prepareMergeBoxDeleteBranch(ctx, canDelete)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}

	prConfig := issue.Repo.MustGetUnit(ctx, unit.TypePullRequests).PullRequestsConfig()
	data.AutodetectManualMerge = prConfig.AutodetectManualMerge

	needRefreshMergeBox := pull.IsChecking()
	needRefreshMergeBox = needRefreshMergeBox || (data.StatusCheckData != nil && data.StatusCheckData.pullCommitStatusState.IsPending())
	data.ReloadingInterval = util.Iif(needRefreshMergeBox, 5000, 0)

	// Only show the merge box if the PR is not merged, or the branch is deletable.
	// Otherwise, there is nothing to do, because the PR view page already contains enough information.
	data.ShowMergeBox = !pull.HasMerged || data.IsPullBranchDeletable

	isRepoAdmin := ctx.IsSigned && (ctx.Repo.Permission.IsAdmin() || ctx.Doer.IsAdmin)

	// admin can merge without checks, writer can merge when checks succeed
	// admin and writer both can make an auto merge schedule (not affected by overridable blockers)
	// Required scoped workflow checks gate the merge even when the rule's own status check is disabled (see IsPullCommitStatusPass),
	// so block on any required status context, not only when enableStatusCheck is on.
	data.hasStatusCheckBlocker = (data.enableStatusCheck || data.hasRequiredStatusContexts) && !data.StatusCheckData.RequiredChecksState.IsSuccess()

	// this logic is from:
	// {{$notAllOverridableChecksOk := or .IsBlockedByApprovals .IsBlockedByRejection .IsBlockedByOfficialReviewRequests .IsBlockedByOutdatedBranch .IsBlockedByChangedProtectedFiles (and .EnableStatusCheck (not $requiredStatusCheckState.IsSuccess))}}
	// HINT: if a PR's status is not mergeable, then it is a non-overridable blocker, such logic is handled separately (see IsStatusMergeable)
	data.hasOverridableBlockers = data.isBlockedByApprovals || data.isBlockedByRejection ||
		data.isBlockedByOfficialReviewRequests || data.isBlockedByOutdatedBranch || data.isBlockedByChangedProtectedFiles ||
		data.hasStatusCheckBlocker

	data.canBypassProtection = isRepoAdmin
	data.canBypassProtectionAsAdmin = isRepoAdmin
	if ctx.IsSigned && prInfo.ProtectedBranchRule != nil {
		data.canBypassProtection = git_model.CanBypassBranchProtection(ctx, prInfo.ProtectedBranchRule, ctx.Doer, isRepoAdmin)
		data.canBypassProtectionAsAdmin = isRepoAdmin && !prInfo.ProtectedBranchRule.BlockAdminMergeOverride
	}

	// CanMergeNow means: if the doer has write permission, whether the PR can be merged now
	data.canMergeNow = (!data.hasOverridableBlockers || data.canBypassProtection) && // status checks are satisfied
		(!data.requireSigned || data.willSign) // signing requirement is satisfied

	prInfo.prepareMergeBoxFormProps(ctx)
	prInfo.prepareMergeBoxInfoItems(ctx)
	prInfo.prepareMergeBoxIconColor()

	ctx.Data["PullMergeBoxData"] = prInfo.MergeBoxData
}

func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) preparePullUpdateActions(ctx *context.Context) {
	pull := prInfo.issue.PullRequest
	data := prInfo.MergeBoxData
	userUpdateStyles, err := pull_service.CheckUserAllowedToUpdate(ctx, pull, ctx.Doer)

			return err
		} else if pr.Issue.IsClosed {
			return ErrIsClosed
		}

		if allowedMerge, err := IsUserAllowedToMerge(ctx, pr, *perm, doer); err != nil {
			log.Error("Error whilst checking if %-v is allowed to merge %-v: %v", doer, pr, err)
			return err

			return nil

		if errProtection := CheckPullBranchProtections(ctx, pr, false); errProtection != nil {
			if !errors.Is(errProtection, ErrNotReadyToMerge) {
				log.Error("Error whilst checking pull branch protection for %-v: %v", pr, errProtection)
				return errProtection
			}

			// Now the branch protection check failed, check whether the failure could be skipped (skip by setting err = nil)

			// * when doing Auto Merge (Scheduled Merge After Checks Succeed), skip the branch protection check
			if mergeCheckType == MergeCheckTypeAuto {
				errProtection = nil
			}

			// * if the doer tries to "Force Merge", check whether it is really allowed
			if forceMerge {
				isRepoAdmin, errForceMerge := access_model.IsUserRepoAdmin(ctx, pr.BaseRepo, doer)
				if errForceMerge != nil {
					return fmt.Errorf("IsUserRepoAdmin failed, repo: %v, doer: %v, err: %w", pr.BaseRepoID, doer.ID, errForceMerge)
				}

				protectedBranchRule, errForceMerge := git_model.GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule(ctx, pr.BaseRepoID, pr.BaseBranch)
				if errForceMerge != nil {
					return fmt.Errorf("GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule failed, repo: %v, base branch: %v, err: %w", pr.BaseRepoID, pr.BaseBranch, errForceMerge)
				}

				canForceMerge := isRepoAdmin
				if protectedBranchRule != nil {
					canForceMerge = git_model.CanBypassBranchProtection(ctx, protectedBranchRule, doer, isRepoAdmin)
				}
				if canForceMerge {
					errProtection = nil
				}
			}

			// If there is still a branch protection check error, return it
			if errProtection != nil {
				return errProtection
			}
		}

		if err := checkSigningRequirements(ctx, pr, doer, mergeStyle); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if err := pr.LoadBaseRepo(ctx); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if pr.BaseRepo.IsDependenciesEnabled(ctx) { // closing skips dependencies too when they are turned off
			if blocked, err := issues_model.MergeBlockedByDependencies(ctx, pr); err != nil {
				return err
			} else if blocked {
				return ErrDependenciesLeft
			}
		}

		return nil
	})
}

// checkSigningRequirements enforces the target branch's RequireSignedCommits rule
// against the selected merge style:
//   - fast-forward-only and merge keep the user's commits on the base branch, so
//     those commits must all be verified, or the pre-receive hook will reject the
//     push with a generic error.
//   - fast-forward-only creates no Gitea commit, so Gitea's signing key is not used.
//   - merge, rebase, rebase-merge and squash produce a Gitea-signed commit, so
//     Gitea must be configured to sign it.

// BlockedByDependencies finds all Dependencies an issue is blocked by
func (issue *Issue) BlockedByDependencies(ctx context.Context, opts db.ListOptions) (issueDeps []*DependencyInfo, total int64, err error) {
	sess := db.GetEngine(ctx).
		Table("issue").
		Join("INNER", "repository", "repository.id = issue.repo_id").
		Join("INNER", "issue_dependency", "issue_dependency.dependency_id = issue.id").
		Where("issue_id = ?", issue.ID).
		// sort by repo id then created date, with the issues of the same repo at the beginning of the list
		OrderBy("CASE WHEN issue.repo_id = ? THEN 0 ELSE issue.repo_id END, issue.created_unix DESC", issue.RepoID)
	if opts.Page > 0 {
		db.SetSessionPagination(sess, &opts)
	}
	total, err = sess.FindAndCount(&issueDeps)

	for _, depInfo := range issueDeps {
		depInfo.Issue.Repo = &depInfo.Repository
	}

	return issueDeps, total, err
}

// BlockingDependencies returns all blocking dependencies, aka all other issues a given issue blocks
func (issue *Issue) BlockingDependencies(ctx context.Context) (issueDeps []*DependencyInfo, err error) {
	err = db.GetEngine(ctx).
		Table("issue").
		Join("INNER", "repository", "repository.id = issue.repo_id").
		Join("INNER", "issue_dependency", "issue_dependency.issue_id = issue.id").
		Where("dependency_id = ?", issue.ID).
		// sort by repo id then created date, with the issues of the same repo at the beginning of the list
		OrderBy("CASE WHEN issue.repo_id = ? THEN 0 ELSE issue.repo_id END, issue.created_unix DESC", issue.RepoID).
		Find(&issueDeps)

	for _, depInfo := range issueDeps {
		depInfo.Issue.Repo = &depInfo.Repository
	}

	return issueDeps, err
}

func migratedIssueCond(tp api.GitServiceType) builder.Cond {
	return builder.In("issue_id",
		builder.Select("issue.id").
			From("issue").
			InnerJoin("repository", "issue.repo_id = repository.id").
			Where(builder.Eq{
				"repository.original_service_type": tp,
			}),
	)
}

func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) prepareMergeBoxProtectionChecks(ctx *context.Context) {
	pb, err := git_model.GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule(ctx, ctx.Repo.Repository.ID, prInfo.issue.PullRequest.BaseBranch)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule", err)
		return
	}
	if pb != nil {
		pb.Repo = prInfo.issue.PullRequest.BaseRepo
		prInfo.ProtectedBranchRule = pb
	}

	prInfo.prepareMergeBoxStatusCheckData(ctx)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}

	prInfo.prepareMergeBoxProtectedRules(ctx)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}
}

func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) prepareMergeBoxProtectedRules(ctx *context.Context) {
	pb := prInfo.ProtectedBranchRule
	if pb == nil {
		return
	}

	pull := prInfo.issue.PullRequest
	data := prInfo.MergeBoxData

	data.isBlockedByApprovals = !issues_model.HasEnoughApprovals(ctx, pb, pull)
	if data.isBlockedByApprovals {
		grantedApprovals := issues_model.GetGrantedApprovalsCount(ctx, pb, pull)
		blockerInfo := ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.blocked_by_approvals", grantedApprovals, pb.RequiredApprovals)
		if pb.EnableApprovalsWhitelist {
			blockerInfo = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.blocked_by_approvals_whitelisted", grantedApprovals, pb.RequiredApprovals)
		}
		data.infoProtectionBlockers.AddErrorItem(blockerInfo)
	}

	data.isBlockedByRejection = issues_model.MergeBlockedByRejectedReview(ctx, pb, pull)
	if data.isBlockedByRejection {
		data.infoProtectionBlockers.AddErrorItem(ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.blocked_by_rejection"))
	}

	data.isBlockedByOfficialReviewRequests = issues_model.MergeBlockedByOfficialReviewRequests(ctx, pb, pull)
	if data.isBlockedByOfficialReviewRequests {
		data.infoProtectionBlockers.AddErrorItem(ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.blocked_by_official_review_requests"))
	}

	data.isBlockedByOutdatedBranch = issues_model.MergeBlockedByOutdatedBranch(pb, pull)
	if data.isBlockedByOutdatedBranch {
		data.infoProtectionBlockers.AddErrorItem(ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.blocked_by_outdated_branch"))
	}

	data.isBlockedByChangedProtectedFiles = len(pull.ChangedProtectedFiles) != 0
	if data.isBlockedByChangedProtectedFiles {
		detailItems := escapeStringSliceToHTML(pull.ChangedProtectedFiles)
		data.infoProtectionBlockers.AddErrorItem(
			ctx.Locale.TrN(len(pull.ChangedProtectedFiles), "repo.pulls.blocked_by_changed_protected_files_1", "repo.pulls.blocked_by_changed_protected_files_n"),
			detailItems,
		)
	}
}

## Where the change goes

```
PR page ─ ViewIssue (routers/web/repo/issue_view.go:370)
  ├─ sidebar: prepareIssueViewSidebarDependency (:456) ──> sidebar/issue_dependencies.tmpl   ← AC5, AC6
  └─ merge box: prepareMergeBox (:867)  (also reloaded alone by ViewPullMergeBox :430)
        ├─ prepareMergeBoxProtectedRules (:1058)  "blocked by approvals…" messages  ← AC1, AC4
        ├─ prepareMergeBoxFormProps (pull_merge_form.go:20)  which merge buttons    ← AC2, AC3
        └─ pull_merge_box.tmpl  just prints what Go prepared
```

How I found it: I searched for `BlockedByDependencies`, which led to the sidebar, and followed `PullMergeBoxData` to the merge box. A note for your React instincts: here the Go code builds the merge box's messages as finished HTML, and the template only prints them. Gitea's own comment asks for this ("let backend handle complex logic", `routers/web/repo/pull.go:325`). That helps D6, because logic in Go can be mutated and logic in templates can't.

There's already a precedent for each part:
- **AC1:** a blocked-by-protected-files message followed by a list (`issue_view.go:1092`). Ours would be a new `repo.pulls.blocked_by_dependencies` next to the other `blocked_by_*` messages.
- **AC2:** a conflicted pull request already offers only "Manually merged" (`pull_merge_form.go:111`, `:161`).
- **AC4:** the existing "You do not have permission to read %d dependency" messages.
- **AC5:** "Open", "Closed" and "Merged" already exist as locale strings, so no new text is needed.

## Staying clear of #149
#149 edits the top of `models/issues/dependency.go` (imports, and the loop check around line 190), locale line 1796, and `.claude-students/docs/models-issues.md`, which is now at its 120-line cap. #144 will:
- add at the end of `dependency.go` and leave its imports alone;
- add its locale key around line 1918;
- put its docs in other pages.

Before the PR I'll do a test merge of both branches to show they combine without conflicts.

## Commit plan (sketch)
1. Model: list the dependencies that block a merge, using the same rule as #143's merge check, with a unit test.
2. Merge box: the "blocked by its dependencies:" message with links, and the count of unreadable ones (AC1, AC4, AC6).
3. Merge box: no merge or auto-merge buttons, "Manually merged" kept, and no "can be merged" message while blocked (AC2, AC3).
4. Sidebar: each dependency's state (AC5).
5. Page-level tests for whatever the unit tests can't reach.
6. Docs.

Then the review, the D6 mutation run, and the PR.

## Decisions needed before commit 1

**1. Where the rule "which dependencies block merging" lives.** The merge box has to list exactly what #143's check refuses, and #143 wrote that rule as a single yes/no database query (`dependency.go:207`).
- **(a)** Pull #143's condition out into one shared piece. #143's yes/no check and a new "list them" query both use it, so there's one rule and two uses.
- **(b)** Rewrite the rule in Go: load the dependencies, then filter them with a Go check. Both #143's check and the page use that check. A merge check then makes two database queries instead of one.
- **(c)** Write a new list query with its own copy of the condition. #143's code stays untouched, but the two copies can drift apart.

I recommend **(a)**. It follows #143 and Gitea, which let the database do this filtering, and it changes the least merged code.

The D6 cost: go-mutesting doesn't mutate database conditions, so under (a) the rule itself gets no mutants. D6's mutants would come from the merge box code, which router unit tests can cover (`pull_review_test.go:33` mocks a PR page). (b) would also put mutants on the rule. Whichever you pick, it should get a written decision, since it has two alternatives.

**2. AC1's link format for a dependency in the same repository.** The AC says "shown as in the timeline: `owner/repo#N - title`". The timeline, though, shows `#N title` for the same repository and `owner/repo#N - title` only for other repositories (`comments.tmpl:346-349`).
- **(a)** Always `owner/repo#N - title`. This matches the AC's literal format and the scenario's "each with its repository and title".
- **(b)** Exactly as the timeline does it, short form for the same repository.

I recommend **(a)**. It fits both the AC text and the scenario, so the issue needs no edit. If you pick (b), AC1's wording should change to match.

I'll bring the look of AC5's state (word only, icon plus word, or a coloured label) when we reach commit 4.

// Copyright 2018 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues_test

import (
	"testing"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestCreateIssueDependency(t *testing.T) {
	// Prepare
	assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())

	issue2Reopened, err := issues_model.GetIssueByID(t.Context(), 2)
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	assert.False(t, issue2Reopened.IsClosed)
}

func TestMergeBlockedByDependencies(t *testing.T) {
	// pull request 2 (issue 3, repo1) gets one dependency, depID, closed first when closeDep is set
	setup := func(t *testing.T, depID int64, closeDep bool) *issues_model.PullRequest {
		require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
		doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 1})
		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2})
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
		dep := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: depID})
		if closeDep {
			_, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), dep, doer, issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{})
			require.NoError(t, err)
		}
		require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(t.Context(), doer, pr.Issue, dep))
		return pr
	}
	assertBlocked := func(t *testing.T, pr *issues_model.PullRequest, expected bool) {
		blocked, err := issues_model.MergeBlockedByDependencies(t.Context(), pr)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, expected, blocked)
	}

	t.Run("OpenIssue", func(t *testing.T) {
		assertBlocked(t, setup(t, 1, false), true)
	})
	t.Run("ClosedIssue", func(t *testing.T) {
		assertBlocked(t, setup(t, 1, true), false)
	})
	t.Run("OpenPull", func(t *testing.T) {
		assertBlocked(t, setup(t, 11, false), true) // pull request 5, not merged
	})
	t.Run("MergedPull", func(t *testing.T) {
		assertBlocked(t, setup(t, 2, true), false) // pull request 1 is merged; closed as a real merge would, the fixture leaves it open
	})
	t.Run("PullClosedWithoutMerging", func(t *testing.T) {
		pr := setup(t, 11, true)
		assertBlocked(t, pr, true)

		// closing pr itself still treats the closed pull request as done
		noDeps, err := issues_model.IssueNoDependenciesLeft(t.Context(), pr.Issue)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.True(t, noDeps)
	})
}
}

// Check if the dependency already exists
func issueDepExists(ctx context.Context, issueID, depID int64) (bool, error) {
	return db.GetEngine(ctx).Where("(issue_id = ? AND dependency_id = ?)", issueID, depID).Exist(&IssueDependency{})
}

// IssueNoDependenciesLeft checks if issue can be closed
func IssueNoDependenciesLeft(ctx context.Context, issue *Issue) (bool, error) {
	exists, err := db.GetEngine(ctx).
		Table("issue_dependency").
		Select("issue.*").
		Join("INNER", "issue", "issue.id = issue_dependency.dependency_id").
		Where("issue_dependency.issue_id = ?", issue.ID).
		And("issue.is_closed = ?", "0").
		Exist(&Issue{})

	return !exists, err
}

// MergeBlockedByDependencies checks if pr depends on an open issue or on a pull request that is not merged.
// Closing ignores whether a pull request was merged (IssueNoDependenciesLeft); merging must not.
func MergeBlockedByDependencies(ctx context.Context, pr *PullRequest) (bool, error) {
	return db.GetEngine(ctx).
		Table("issue_dependency").
		Select("issue.*").
		Join("INNER", "issue", "issue.id = issue_dependency.dependency_id").
		Join("LEFT", "pull_request", "pull_request.issue_id = issue.id").
		Where("issue_dependency.issue_id = ?", pr.IssueID).
		And(builder.Or(
			builder.Eq{"issue.is_closed": false},
			builder.Eq{"pull_request.has_merged": false}, // NULL for an issue, so only a pull request matches
		)).
		Exist(&Issue{})
}

func migratedIssueCond(tp api.GitServiceType) builder.Cond {
	return builder.In("issue_id",
		builder.Select("issue.id").
			From("issue").
			InnerJoin("repository", "issue.repo_id = repository.id").
			Where(builder.Eq{
				"repository.original_service_type": tp,
			}),
	)
}

# Issue #144 design decisions (one per commit, posted by @ab-wm)


## Commit 1 Design Decision - @ab-wm
### Decision 1: The merge box and the merge check share one rule for which dependencies block merging

**Decision:** The rule from #143 (an open issue or pull request, or a pull request closed without merging, blocks a merge) is kept in one place. The merge check uses it to answer "is this pull request blocked?", and the pull request page uses it to list the dependencies that block it.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Rewrite the rule as a check run on each dependency after loading them all, and use that check in both places. (b) Give the page its own list with a copy of the rule.
**Rationale:** The merge box should name exactly the dependencies the merge check refuses, and with one rule the two cannot disagree. As in #143, the database picks out the blocking dependencies, so the merge check still asks a single question. (a) would load every dependency only to set most of them aside, and (b) would leave two copies that drift apart when only one of them is changed.
**Consequences:** #143's merge check now runs on the shared rule, so its existing tests also check this change. Changing what blocks a merge later changes the merge check and the page together.

```

+// GetMergeBlockingDependencies returns the dependencies that block merging pr, each with its repository loaded.
+func GetMergeBlockingDependencies(ctx context.Context, pr *PullRequest) (issueDeps []*DependencyInfo, err error) {
+	err = db.GetEngine(ctx).
+		Table("issue").
+		Join("INNER", "repository", "repository.id = issue.repo_id").
+		Join("INNER", "issue_dependency", "issue_dependency.dependency_id = issue.id").
+		Where("issue_dependency.issue_id = ?", pr.IssueID).
+		And(mergeBlockingDependencyCond()).
+		Find(&issueDeps)
+
+	for _, depInfo := range issueDeps {
+		depInfo.Issue.Repo = &depInfo.Repository
+	}
+
+	return issueDeps, err
+}
+
+// mergeBlockingDependencyCond matches an open issue or pull request, or a pull request closed without merging.
+// Shared so the merge check and the merge box list the same dependencies.
+func mergeBlockingDependencyCond() builder.Cond {
+	return builder.Or(
+		builder.Eq{"issue.is_closed": false},
+		builder.In("issue.id", builder.Select("issue_id").From("pull_request").Where(builder.Eq{"has_merged": false})),
+	)
+}

I've staged commit 1; the commit is yours to make. First, your question.

## Question 2: the best link format, setting the issue aside

Show the repository only for a dependency in another repository: `#9 title` for the same repository, `owner/repo#9 - title` for another one. That's what the timeline does. My reasons:
- **It's Gitea's rule everywhere.** Timeline dependency events (`comments.tmpl:346-349`), "referenced from" events (`comments.tmpl:147`), and issue lists, which add `owner/repo` only on the dashboard, where items come from many repositories (`issuelist_items.tmpl:46`).
- **The merge box is part of the timeline.** It's the timeline's last item, just below the "added a new dependency" events it would be repeating.
- **Less noise.** Most dependencies are in the same repository. Repeating `owner/repo` on every line tells the reader nothing new, and `#9` alone always means this repository.

The cost is that a list mixing both kinds shows two formats, the same as the timeline already does.

If you take it, the issue needs two edits:
- **AC1:** "…followed by a link to each blocking dependency, shown as in the timeline: `#N title` for one in the same repository, `owner/repo#N - title` for one in another repository."
- **Scenario:** "followed by links to #11 and #9, each with its repository and title" becomes "followed by links to #11 and #9 with their titles".

The spec review asked exactly this question, so a one-line comment to @controlled-opposition about the change may be worth adding. That's your call. Commit 2 waits on your answer.

- **`models/issues/dependency_test.go`:** one new test, added at the end of the file. It gives a pull request one dependency of each kind in the issue's table and checks which ones are listed and which repository each belongs to.

func TestCheckPullMergeableDependencies(t *testing.T) {
	// user2 owns repo1 and could merge pull request 2, which gets one dependency, depID, closed first when closeDep is set
	check := func(t *testing.T, depID int64, closeDep, dependenciesEnabled bool) error {
		require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
		ctx := t.Context()
		doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2})
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(ctx))
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadBaseRepo(ctx))

		dep := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: depID})
		if closeDep {
			_, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(ctx, dep, doer, issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{})
			require.NoError(t, err)
		}
		require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(ctx, doer, pr.Issue, dep))

		issuesUnit, err := pr.BaseRepo.GetUnit(ctx, unit.TypeIssues)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		issuesUnit.IssuesConfig().EnableDependencies = dependenciesEnabled // fixture repos leave it unset, which reads as off
		require.NoError(t, repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig(ctx, issuesUnit))

		pr = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2}) // reload, so the setting comes from the database
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadBaseRepo(ctx))
		perm, err := access_model.GetDoerRepoPermission(ctx, pr.BaseRepo, doer)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		return CheckPullMergeable(ctx, doer, &perm, pr, MergeCheckTypeGeneral, repo_model.MergeStyleMerge, false)
	}

	t.Run("OpenIssue", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.ErrorIs(t, check(t, 1, false, true), ErrDependenciesLeft)
	})
	t.Run("ClosedIssue", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.NoError(t, check(t, 1, true, true))
	})
	t.Run("PullClosedWithoutMerging", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.ErrorIs(t, check(t, 11, true, true), ErrDependenciesLeft) // pull request 5
	})
	t.Run("MergedPull", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.NoError(t, check(t, 2, true, true)) // pull request 1 is merged; closed as a real merge would, the fixture leaves it open
	})
	t.Run("DependenciesTurnedOff", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.NoError(t, check(t, 11, true, false))
	})
}

```text
// Copyright 2020 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package translation

import (
	"fmt"
	"html"
	"html/template"
)

// MockLocale provides a mocked locale without any translations
type MockLocale struct {
	Lang, LangName string // these fields are used directly in templates: ctx.Locale.Lang
}

var _ Locale = (*MockLocale)(nil)

func (l MockLocale) Language() string {
	return "en"
}

func (l MockLocale) TrString(format string, args ...any) (ret string) {
	ret = format + ":"
	for _, arg := range args {
		// usually there is no arg or at most 1-2 args, so a simple string concatenation is more efficient
		switch v := arg.(type) {
		case string:
			ret += v + ","
		default:
			ret += fmt.Sprint(v) + ","
		}
	}
	return ret[:len(ret)-1]
}

func (l MockLocale) Tr(format string, args ...any) (ret template.HTML) {
	ret = template.HTML(html.EscapeString(format)) + ":"
	for _, arg := range args {
		// usually there is no arg or at most 1-2 args, so a simple string concatenation is more efficient
		switch v := arg.(type) {
		case template.HTML:
			ret += v + ","
		case string:
			ret += template.HTML(html.EscapeString(v)) + ","
		default:
			ret += template.HTML(html.EscapeString(fmt.Sprint(v))) + ","
		}
	}
	return ret[:len(ret)-1]
}

func (l MockLocale) TrN(cnt any, key1, keyN string, args ...any) template.HTML {
	return l.Tr(key1, args...)
}

func (l MockLocale) PrettyNumber(v any) string {
	return fmt.Sprint(v)
}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package repo

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	"gitea.dev/models/unit"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/translation"
	"gitea.dev/services/contexttest"

	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestPrepareMergeBoxDependencies(t *testing.T) {
	translation.InitLocales(t.Context()) // the expected texts are the English ones

	// viewerID opens pull request 2 (issue 3 in user2/repo1) after user2 gives it the dependencies depIDs.
	// It returns the merge box's blockers as text: each message, then each of its list entries as "text -> link".
	blockers := func(t *testing.T, viewerID int64, dependenciesEnabled bool, depIDs ...int64) []string {
		require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
		owner := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2})
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
		for _, depID := range depIDs {
			dep := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: depID})
			require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(t.Context(), owner, pr.Issue, dep))
		}
		repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
		issuesUnit, err := repo.GetUnit(t.Context(), unit.TypeIssues)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		issuesUnit.IssuesConfig().EnableDependencies = dependenciesEnabled // fixture repos leave it unset, which reads as off
		require.NoError(t, repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig(t.Context(), issuesUnit))

		ctx, _ := contexttest.MockContext(t, "user2/repo1/pulls/2")
		ctx.Locale = translation.NewLocale("en-US")
		contexttest.LoadUser(t, ctx, viewerID)
		contexttest.LoadRepo(t, ctx, 1)
		prInfo := &pullRequestViewInfo{issue: pr.Issue, MergeBoxData: &pullMergeBoxData{}}
		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxDependencies(ctx)
		require.False(t, ctx.Written())

		texts := []string{}
		for _, item := range prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.items {
			texts = append(texts, string(item.InfoHTML))
			for _, listItem := range item.ListItems {
				doc, err := goquery.NewDocumentFromReader(strings.NewReader(string(listItem)))
				require.NoError(t, err)
				text := strings.TrimSpace(doc.Text())
				if href, ok := doc.Find("a").Attr("href"); ok {
					text += " -> " + href
				}
				texts = append(texts, text)
			}
		}
		return texts
	}

	t.Run("AC1 links each blocking dependency", func(t *testing.T) {
		// issue 1 (#1) is in the same repository, issue 7 (#2) in user2/repo2
		texts := blockers(t, 2, true, 1, 7)
		require.NotEmpty(t, texts)
		assert.Equal(t, "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:", texts[0])
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
			"#1 issue1 -> /user2/repo1/issues/1",
			"user2/repo2#2 - issue7 -> /user2/repo2/issues/2",
		}, texts[1:])
	})
	t.Run("AC3 no dependencies", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.Empty(t, blockers(t, 2, true))
	})
	t.Run("AC4 counts a dependency the viewer cannot read", func(t *testing.T) {
		// user4 can read the public user2/repo1 but not the private user2/repo2
		texts := blockers(t, 4, true, 1, 7)
		require.NotEmpty(t, texts)
		assert.Equal(t, "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:", texts[0])
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
			"#1 issue1 -> /user2/repo1/issues/1",
			"You do not have permission to read 1 dependency",
		}, texts[1:])
	})
	t.Run("AC6 dependencies turned off", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.Empty(t, blockers(t, 2, false, 1, 7))
	})
}

**Question 3: the message while the branch has conflicts.** The merge box shows either the problems with the branch itself (conflicts, the branch already being in the base, a check still running) or the other blockers (approvals, protected files, and now dependencies), never both (`pull_merge_box.go:218`). // Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package repo

import (
	"strings"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	"gitea.dev/models/unit"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"

	"gitea.dev/modules/translation"
	"gitea.dev/services/context"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"

// mockPullWithDependencies opens pull request 2 (issue 3 in user2/repo1) as viewerID, after user2 gives it the dependencies depIDs.
// It loads the real English locale, as the expected texts are the English ones.
func mockPullWithDependencies(t *testing.T, viewerID int64, dependenciesEnabled bool, depIDs ...int64) (*context.Context, *pullRequestViewInfo) {
	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
	translation.InitLocales(t.Context())
	owner := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
	pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2})
	require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
	for _, depID := range depIDs {
		dep := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: depID})
		require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(t.Context(), owner, pr.Issue, dep))
	}
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	issuesUnit, err := repo.GetUnit(t.Context(), unit.TypeIssues)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	issuesUnit.IssuesConfig().EnableDependencies = dependenciesEnabled // fixture repos leave it unset, which reads as off
	require.NoError(t, repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig(t.Context(), issuesUnit))

	ctx, _ := contexttest.MockContext(t, "user2/repo1/pulls/2")
	ctx.Locale = translation.NewLocale("en-US")
	contexttest.LoadUser(t, ctx, viewerID)
	contexttest.LoadRepo(t, ctx, 1)
	return ctx, &pullRequestViewInfo{issue: pr.Issue, MergeBoxData: &pullMergeBoxData{}}
}

func TestPrepareMergeBoxDependencies(t *testing.T) {
	// the merge box's blockers as text: each message, then each of its list entries as "text -> link"
	blockers := func(t *testing.T, viewerID int64, dependenciesEnabled bool, depIDs ...int64) []string {
		ctx, prInfo := mockPullWithDependencies(t, viewerID, dependenciesEnabled, depIDs...)
		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxDependencies(ctx)
		require.False(t, ctx.Written())

		texts := []string{}
		for _, item := range prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.items {
			texts = append(texts, string(item.InfoHTML))
			for _, listItem := range item.ListItems {
				doc, err := goquery.NewDocumentFromReader(strings.NewReader(string(listItem)))
				require.NoError(t, err)
				text := strings.TrimSpace(doc.Text())
				if href, ok := doc.Find("a").Attr("href"); ok {
					text += " -> " + href
				}
				texts = append(texts, text)
			}
		}
		return texts
	}

	t.Run("AC1 links each blocking dependency", func(t *testing.T) {
		// issue 1 (#1) is in the same repository, issue 7 (#2) in user2/repo2
		texts := blockers(t, 2, true, 1, 7)
		require.NotEmpty(t, texts)
		assert.Equal(t, "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:", texts[0])
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
			"#1 issue1 -> /user2/repo1/issues/1",
			"user2/repo2#2 - issue7 -> /user2/repo2/issues/2",
		}, texts[1:])
	})
	t.Run("AC3 no dependencies", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.Empty(t, blockers(t, 2, true))
	})
	t.Run("AC4 counts a dependency the viewer cannot read", func(t *testing.T) {
		// user4 can read the public user2/repo1 but not the private user2/repo2
		texts := blockers(t, 4, true, 1, 7)
		require.NotEmpty(t, texts)
		assert.Equal(t, "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:", texts[0])
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
			"#1 issue1 -> /user2/repo1/issues/1",
			"You do not have permission to read 1 dependency",
		}, texts[1:])
	})
	t.Run("AC6 dependencies turned off", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.Empty(t, blockers(t, 2, false, 1, 7))
	})
}

func TestPrepareMergeBoxFormWithDependencies(t *testing.T) {
	type offer struct {
		styles   []string // the merge styles offered, "+auto" where "(When checks succeed)" is offered with it; nil when there is no merge form
		messages []string
	}
	// user2 owns user2/repo1 and may merge pull request 2, whose branch merges cleanly. checksPending holds the merge back
	// for status checks user2 cannot bypass, which is when "(When checks succeed)" is offered.
	mergeBox := func(t *testing.T, allowManualMerge, checksPending bool, depIDs ...int64) offer {
		ctx, prInfo := mockPullWithDependencies(t, 2, true, depIDs...)
		contexttest.LoadGitRepo(t, ctx)
		defer ctx.Repo.GitRepo.Close()
		ctx.Repo.Repository.MustGetUnit(ctx, unit.TypePullRequests).PullRequestsConfig().AllowManualMerge = allowManualMerge
		data := prInfo.MergeBoxData
		data.hasPermToMerge = true
		data.hasOverridableBlockers = checksPending
		data.canMergeNow = !checksPending

		// in the order prepareMergeBox runs them
		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxDependencies(ctx)
		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxFormProps(ctx)
		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxInfoItems(ctx)
		require.False(t, ctx.Written())

		var o offer
		if data.MergeFormProps != nil {
			for _, s := range data.MergeFormProps["mergeStyles"].([]any) {
				style := s.(map[string]any)
				if !style["allowed"].(bool) {
					continue
				}
				name := style["name"].(string)
				if !style["hideAutoMerge"].(bool) {
					name += "+auto"
				}
				o.styles = append(o.styles, name)
			}
		}
		for _, section := range data.InfoSections {
			for _, item := range section.InfoItems {
				o.messages = append(o.messages, string(item.InfoHTML))
			}
		}
		return o
	}

	t.Run("AC2 only Manually merged while blocked", func(t *testing.T) {
		o := mergeBox(t, true, false, 1)
		assert.Equal(t, []string{"manually-merged"}, o.styles)
		assert.NotContains(t, o.messages, "This pull request can be merged automatically.")
	})
	t.Run("AC2 no merge form while blocked and waiting for checks", func(t *testing.T) {
		o := mergeBox(t, false, true, 1)
		assert.Nil(t, o.styles)
		assert.NotContains(t, o.messages, "This pull request cannot be merged because all repository merge options are disabled.")
	})
	t.Run("control: waiting for checks offers (When checks succeed)", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.Contains(t, mergeBox(t, false, true).styles, "merge+auto")
	})
	t.Run("AC3 resolved dependencies look as with none", func(t *testing.T) {
		none := mergeBox(t, false, false)
		assert.Equal(t, []string{"merge", "rebase", "rebase-merge", "squash"}, none.styles) // the styles user2/repo1 allows
		assert.Contains(t, none.messages, "This pull request can be merged automatically.")
		assert.Equal(t, none, mergeBox(t, false, false, 5)) // issue 5 is closed
	})
}

```

func (issues IssueList) LoadPullRequests(ctx context.Context) error {
	issuesIDs := issues.getPullIssueIDs()
	if len(issuesIDs) == 0 {
		return nil
	}

	pullRequestMaps := make(map[int64]*PullRequest, len(issuesIDs))
	left := len(issuesIDs)
	for left > 0 {
		limit := min(left, db.DefaultMaxInSize)
		rows, err := db.GetEngine(ctx).

			Rows(new(PullRequest))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

			var pr PullRequest

			if err != nil {

(a) word only           (b) icon + word              (c) coloured label
#11 Fix login            ⊗ #11 Fix login             #11 Fix login   [Closed] 🗑
user2/repo1 · Closed     user2/repo1 · Closed        user2/repo1
#9 Crash on save         ◉ #9 Crash on save          #9 Crash on save  [Open] 🗑
user2/repo1 · Open       user2/repo1 · Open          user2/repo1
```

- **(a)** The word on the grey repository line. This is the smallest change.
- **(b)** Gitea's own state icon in front of the title, plus the word on the grey line. The icons are the ones the issue lists use, and they come from the existing `shared/issueicon` partial:
  - green for open;
  - purple merge icon for merged;
  - red for closed, or the close-reason icon your team added.
- **(c)** A small coloured label with the word, like the "Open" or "Merged" label at the top of an issue page, placed at the entry's right next to the trash icon.

I recommend **(b)**. The colour makes merged against closed visible at a glance, which is the problem the scenario describes. The word satisfies AC5 literally and tells a merged pull request (purple) apart from a closed-as-completed issue (also purple). And it reuses the existing icon partial instead of adding new markup. (c) crowds an already narrow sidebar, where titles get cut off.

All three keep the strike-through on closed and merged titles, since AC5 doesn't ask to change it. Tell me if this choice deserves a written decision. I'd say it doesn't if you pick (b), because it reuses Gitea's existing look.

**How I'll test it:** a unit test that runs the sidebar's data step and renders the real sidebar template, the way `pull_review_test.go:33` already renders a template, then reads each entry's state word. It will cover an open issue, a closed issue, a merged pull request and a pull request closed without merging, in both the "Depends on" and the "Blocks" lists.

func TestIssueViewSidebarDependencyStates(t *testing.T) {
	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
	translation.InitLocales(t.Context()) // the expected texts are the English ones
	owner := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	issuesUnit, err := repo.GetUnit(t.Context(), unit.TypeIssues)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	issuesUnit.IssuesConfig().EnableDependencies = true // fixture repos leave it unset, which reads as off
	require.NoError(t, repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig(t.Context(), issuesUnit))

	// in user2/repo1: issue 1 (#1) open, issue 2 (#2) merged pull request 1, issue 3 (#3) open pull request 2,
	// issue 5 (#4) closed in the fixtures, issue 11 (#5) pull request 5 closed without merging; issue 7 is #2 in the private user2/repo2
	for _, id := range []int64{2, 11} { // pull request 1 is merged but the fixture leaves it open, so close it as a real merge would
		_, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: id}), owner, issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{})
		require.NoError(t, err)
	}
	for _, dep := range [][2]int64{{3, 1}, {3, 2}, {3, 5}, {3, 11}, {3, 7}, {2, 1}, {5, 1}, {11, 1}} { // {issue, the issue it depends on}
		issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: dep[0]})
		require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(t.Context(), owner, issue, unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: dep[1]})))
	}

	// the entries of one sidebar list ("Depends on" or "Blocks") on issueID's page, as viewerID reads them
	sidebarList := func(t *testing.T, viewerID, issueID int64, heading string) []string {
		ctx, resp := contexttest.MockContext(t, "/", contexttest.MockContextOption{Render: templates.PageRenderer()})
		ctx.Locale = translation.NewLocale("en-US")
		contexttest.LoadUser(t, ctx, viewerID)
		contexttest.LoadRepo(t, ctx, 1)
		issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: issueID})
		require.NoError(t, issue.LoadRepo(ctx))
		ctx.Data["Issue"] = issue
		ctx.Data["Repository"] = ctx.Repo.Repository

		prepareIssueViewSidebarDependency(ctx, issue)
		require.False(t, ctx.Written())
		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, "repo/issue/sidebar/issue_dependencies")

		doc, err := goquery.NewDocumentFromReader(resp.Body)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		entries := []string{}
		doc.Find("strong").FilterFunction(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) bool { return s.Text() == heading }).
			Parent().Next().Find(".item").Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
			entries = append(entries, strings.Join(strings.Fields(s.Text()), " "))
		})
		return entries
	}

	t.Run("AC5 Depends on", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
			"#1 issue1 user2/repo1 · Open",
			"#2 issue2 user2/repo1 · Merged",
			"#4 issue5 user2/repo1 · Closed",
			"#5 pull5 user2/repo1 · Closed",
			"#2 issue7 user2/repo2 · Open",
		}, sidebarList(t, 2, 3, "Depends on"))
	})
	t.Run("AC5 Blocks", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
			"#3 issue3 user2/repo1 · Open",
			"#2 issue2 user2/repo1 · Merged",
			"#4 issue5 user2/repo1 · Closed",
			"#5 pull5 user2/repo1 · Closed",
		}, sidebarList(t, 2, 1, "Blocks"))
	})
	t.Run("AC5 an entry the viewer can remove but not read", func(t *testing.T) {
		// user40 may write to user2/repo1, so it manages dependencies, but cannot read user2/repo2
		assert.Contains(t, sidebarList(t, 40, 3, "Depends on"), "#2 issue7 user2/repo2 · Open")
	})
}

## Commit 5: page-level tests

**What the unit tests already cover:** every AC has at least one unit test.
- The merge box's data, which is the message, the links, the unreadable count and which merge styles are offered (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC6).
- The real sidebar template, rendered in English (AC5).

**What no automated test reaches yet:**
1. **The call that adds the dependency message to the merge box** (`issue_view.go`, inside `prepareMergeBox`). The unit tests call the new step directly, so deleting that one line would break the page while every test still passed.
2. **The Vue merge form.** It builds the actual buttons from the data the unit tests check. So "no merge button is offered" (AC2) is only checked one step before what the user sees.

So far only my manual page checks cover these two.

**What's available:** `tests/e2e/utils.ts` already has helpers that create a repo, a branch with a file, a pull request and an issue through the API. CI runs the e2e tests whenever Go or template files change (`pull-e2e-tests.yml:18`). I'll run them locally against my server the same way #143's checks were run.

**Question 5: browser tests.** The issue's Scope says "with browser tests for both parts".
- **(a) Two browser tests:**
  - The merge box: AC1's message and links, and AC2, where only "Manually merged" is offered once the form has loaded.
  - The sidebar: AC5's states.

  This matches the Scope text as written.
- **(b) One browser test, for the merge box only.** It covers both gaps above. A sidebar browser test would mostly repeat the unit test, which already renders the real sidebar template. The Scope line would need editing to something like "with a browser test for the merge box".
- **(c) No browser tests.** The two gaps stay covered only by manual checks, listed as "manual" in Test Evidence, and the Scope line would need editing.

I recommend **(b)**. It closes the only real gaps for one test's cost, and AGENTS.md prefers unit tests where they're enough. If you'd rather keep Scope's wording untouched, (a) adds one more test of about the same size.

Either way, each test creates its own repository through the API. I'll time them and aim for under 2 s each, per AGENTS.md. To avoid a test that passes before the form has even loaded, the merge-box test turns on "Manually merged" for its repository, waits for that button to appear, and only then checks that no other merge option is offered.

None of this affects D6: the mutation tool only runs the Go tests in the package it changes, never the browser tests.

export function baseUrl() {
  return env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_URL?.replace(/\/$/g, '');
}

function apiAuthHeader(username: string, password: string) {
  return {Authorization: `Basic ${globalThis.btoa(`${username}:${password}`)}`};
}

export function apiHeaders() {
  return apiAuthHeader(env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD);
}

async function apiRetry(fn: () => Promise<{ok: () => boolean; status: () => number; text: () => Promise<string>}>, label: string) {
  const maxAttempts = 5;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    const response = await fn();
    if (response.ok()) return;
    if ([500, 502, 503].includes(response.status()) && attempt < maxAttempts - 1) {
      const jitter = Math.random() * 500;
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000 * (attempt + 1) + jitter));
      continue;
    }
    throw new Error(`${label} failed: ${response.status()} ${await response.text()}`);
  }
}

export async function apiCreateRepo(requestContext: APIRequestContext, {name, autoInit = true, headers}: {name: string; autoInit?: boolean; headers?: Record<string, string>}) {
  await apiRetry(() => requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/user/repos`, {
    headers: headers || apiHeaders(),
    data: {name, auto_init: autoInit},
  }), 'apiCreateRepo');
}

export async function apiEditRepo(requestContext: APIRequestContext, owner: string, name: string, data: Record<string, unknown>) {
  await apiRetry(() => requestContext.patch(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${name}`, {
    headers: apiHeaders(),
    data,
  }), 'apiEditRepo');
}

export async function apiCreateFile(requestContext: APIRequestContext, owner: string, repo: string, filepath: string, content: string, {branch, newBranch, message}: {branch?: string; newBranch?: string; message?: string} = {}) {
  await apiRetry(() => requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/contents/${filepath}`, {
    headers: apiHeaders(),
    data: {content: Buffer.from(content, 'utf8').toString('base64'), branch, new_branch: newBranch, message},
  }), 'apiCreateFile');
}

export async function apiCreateBranch(requestContext: APIRequestContext, owner: string, repo: string, newBranch: string) {
  await apiRetry(() => requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/branches`, {
    headers: apiHeaders(),
    data: {new_branch_name: newBranch},
  }), 'apiCreateBranch');
}

/** Create a PR via API. Returns the PR index for subsequent operations. */
export async function apiCreatePR(requestContext: APIRequestContext, owner: string, repo: string, head: string, base: string, title: string, {headers}: {headers?: Record<string, string>} = {}): Promise<number> {
  let prIndex = 0;
  await apiRetry(async () => {
    const response = await requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/pulls`, {
      headers: headers || apiHeaders(),
      data: {head, base, title},
    });
    if (response.ok()) prIndex = (await response.json()).number;
    return response;
  }, 'apiCreatePR');
  return prIndex;
}

/** Create a review on a PR. `event: "COMMENT"` submits immediately without a pending review. */
export async function apiCreateIssue(
  requestContext: APIRequestContext,
  {owner, repo, title, body, projects, milestone, headers}: {
    owner: string;
    repo: string;
    title: string;
    body?: string;
    projects?: number[];
    milestone?: number;
    headers?: Record<string, string>;
  },
): Promise<{index: number}> {
  let result: {index: number} = {index: 0};
  await apiRetry(async () => {
    const response = await requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/issues`, {
      headers: headers || apiHeaders(),
      data: {title, body: body || '', projects: projects || [], ...(milestone && {milestone})},
    });
    if (response.ok()) {
      const json = await response.json();
      // API returns "number" field for the issue index
      result = {index: json.number};
    }
    return response;
  }, 'apiCreateIssue');
  return result;
}

export async function loginUser(page: Page, username: string) {
  return login(page, username, testUserPassword);
}

export async function login(page: Page, username = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, password = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD) {
  const response = await page.request.post('/user/login', {
    form: {user_name: username, password},
    maxRedirects: 0,
  });
  const status = response.status();
  if (status !== 302 && status !== 303) throw new Error(`login as ${username} failed: HTTP ${status}`);
}

export async function assertNoJsError(page: Page) {
  await expect(page.locator('.js-global-error')).toHaveCount(0);

import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import type {APIRequestContext} from '@playwright/test';
import {apiCreateFile, apiCreateIssue, apiCreatePR, apiCreateRepo, apiEditRepo, apiHeaders, baseUrl, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';

const owner = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;

// a repository whose issues can have dependencies, set here rather than left to the server's default
async function createRepoWithDependencies(request: APIRequestContext, name: string, extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}) {
  await apiCreateRepo(request, {name});
  await apiEditRepo(request, owner, name, {
    has_issues: true, // the API ignores internal_tracker without it
    internal_tracker: {enable_time_tracker: true, allow_only_contributors_to_track_time: true, enable_issue_dependencies: true},
    ...extra,
  });
}

async function createPull(request: APIRequestContext, repo: string, branch: string, title: string) {
  await apiCreateFile(request, owner, repo, `${branch}.txt`, `${branch}\n`, {newBranch: branch});
  return apiCreatePR(request, owner, repo, branch, 'main', title);
}

async function addDependency(request: APIRequestContext, repo: string, index: number, dependsOn: number) {
  const response = await request.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${index}/dependencies`, {
    headers: apiHeaders(),
    data: {owner, repo, index: dependsOn},
  });
  expect(response.ok()).toBeTruthy();
}

test('#144 AC1 AC2 the merge box names the blocking dependency and offers only Manually merged', async ({page, request}) => {
  const repo = `e2e-merge-deps-${randomString(8)}`;
  await createRepoWithDependencies(request, repo, {allow_manual_merge: true});
  const pull = await createPull(request, repo, 'blocked', 'Blocked pull');
  const {index: issue} = await apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo, title: 'Open dependency'});
  await Promise.all([addDependency(request, repo, pull, issue), login(page)]);

  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repo}/pulls/${pull}`);
  const mergeBox = page.locator('.pull-merge-box');
  await expect(mergeBox.getByText('This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(mergeBox.getByRole('link', {name: `#${issue} Open dependency`})).toHaveAttribute('href', `/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${issue}`);

  // wait for the merge form to load before checking what it offers, so an empty form cannot pass
  await expect(mergeBox.getByRole('button', {name: 'Manually merged'})).toBeVisible();
  await mergeBox.locator('.merge-button .dropdown').click();
  await expect(mergeBox.locator('.merge-button .menu .item')).toHaveText(['Manually merged']); // no other style, no "(When checks succeed)"
});

test('#144 AC5 the sidebar shows each dependency as Open, Closed or Merged', async ({page, request}) => {
  const repo = `e2e-dep-states-${randomString(8)}`;
  await createRepoWithDependencies(request, repo);
  const {index: subject} = await apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo, title: 'Subject'});
  const [{index: open}, closed, merged] = await Promise.all([
    apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo, title: 'Open issue'}),
    createPull(request, repo, 'closed', 'Closed pull'),
    createPull(request, repo, 'merged', 'Merged pull'),
  ]);
  const pulls = `${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/pulls`;
  expect((await request.patch(`${pulls}/${closed}`, {headers: apiHeaders(), data: {state: 'closed'}})).ok()).toBeTruthy();
  await expect(async () => { // the merge is refused until the new pull request's conflict check has finished
    expect((await request.post(`${pulls}/${merged}/merge`, {headers: apiHeaders(), data: {Do: 'merge'}})).ok()).toBeTruthy();
  }).toPass();
  await Promise.all([
    ...[open, closed, merged].map((dep) => addDependency(request, repo, subject, dep)),
    login(page),
  ]);

  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${subject}`);
  const entries = page.locator('.ui.depending .item.dependency');

```text
---
scope: services/pull, services/gitdiff, services/automerge, services/automergequeue, services/agit
verified-at: 6c8e682391
---

# services/pull and services/gitdiff — pull requests, review, diffs

**Read when:** touching PR creation, mergeability, merging, code review comments, or the diff
viewer.
**Not here:** the `PullRequest` row -> `models-issues.md`; issue-side logic -> `services-issue.md`.
  the merge-style files operate there; only on success is the result pushed. A merge path that
  writes to the real repo directly is a bug.
- Merge styles are `repo_model.MergeStyle` values (`MergeStyleMerge`, `MergeStyleRebase`,
  `MergeStyleRebaseMerge`, `MergeStyleSquash`, `MergeStyleFastForwardOnly`) and each must be
  allowed by the repo's PR unit config — check with the unit accessors
  (`models-repo-and-git.md`), never by string comparison.
- `Merge` is not the permission check. `IsUserAllowedToMerge` and `CheckPullBranchProtections` sit
  beside it in `merge.go` but are separate calls the caller must make itself.
- **Merging and closing judge dependencies differently.** `CheckPullMergeable`
  (`services/pull/check.go`), which the web, API and automerge paths all call, returns
  `ErrDependenciesLeft` while `MergeBlockedByDependencies` (`models/issues/dependency.go`) finds an
  open issue or an unmerged pull request, and skips that check when `IsDependenciesEnabled` is off.
  Closing (`SetIssueAsClosed`, `models/issues/issue_update.go`) skips dependencies the same way and
  otherwise uses `IssueNoDependenciesLeft`, where a closed pull request counts as done. Changing one
  rule does not change the other.
- **Review comments are anchored to a commit, not to a line of the current head.** `CreateCodeComment`
  takes `latestCommitID` and a `treePath`; when the branch moves, `InvalidateCodeComments` marks
  the ones that no longer apply. A comment feature that stores only a line number will drift.
- `GetDiffForRender` and `GetDiffForAPI` are deliberately separate — the render path carries
  highlighting, escaping and a repo link for building URLs. Do not use the API one to build HTML.
- `notify_service.*` is called after the transaction, exactly as in `services-issue.md`.

## Recipes

**Add something to the diff viewer.** Extend `DiffFile`/`DiffSection`/`DiffLine` in
`services/gitdiff/gitdiff.go`, populate it in `ParsePatch` or `GetDiffForRender`, then render it in
----
  `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }`. Without it the test DB is never
  initialised.
- Every DB-backed test calls `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()` first, which reloads the fixtures, so
  tests do not depend on each other's writes.
- Adding a row to `models/fixtures/*.yml` means keeping denormalised counter columns
  (`num_issues`, `num_closed_issues`, ...) consistent, or `CheckConsistencyFor` fails.
- Handler tests use `contexttest.MockContext` rather than constructing a `context.Context`
  by hand — see `services/context` for what the real one carries.
- Integration tests need Git LFS installed. The database comes from `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE`; empty
  defaults to SQLite, which is what you want locally.
- Frontend tests are Vitest, not Jest. Playwright is only for the e2e tier.

## Recipes

**Run one test.**

```sh
go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/   # or: make test-backend#TestName
pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>
GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e
```

**Add a DB-backed unit test.** Put `*_test.go` beside the code; add `main_test.go` with
`unittest.MainTest(m)` if the package has none; call `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()`; load rows
with `unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean`; add fixture rows only if no existing row fits.

**Add an integration test.** New `tests/integration/<feature>_test.go`; `defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()`
at the top of the test; drive it through HTTP the way the neighbouring tests do. Do not add a
`TestMain` — `integration_test.go` already owns it.

**Check a flash message in an integration test.** After the request,
`session.GetCookieFlashMessage().ErrorMsg` (`tests/integration/integration_test.go`) holds the
rendered text. Compare the exact string: a missing locale key renders as the key and then fails.

**Add a migration test.** Alongside the migration in `models/migrations/`, with its own fixtures
under `models/migrations/fixtures/`; helpers in `models/migrations/migrationtest/`.

## Gotchas

- `GITEA_TEST_LOG_SQL=1` logs every SQL statement — the fastest way to see what a failing DB test
  actually queried.
- Fixture repos leave `EnableDependencies` out of their issues config (`models/fixtures/repo_unit.yml`),
  so dependencies read as off and block nothing. A test that needs them turns them on with
  `repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig` (`tests/integration/pull_merge_dependency_test.go`).
- `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR` multiplies e2e timeouts (default 4 on CI, 1 locally); a test that
  only passes with a raised factor is a flaky test, not a slow machine.
- A handful of Go unit tests fail on native Windows for platform reasons (symlinks, temp-file
  cleanup). Run the suite on Linux, macOS, WSL2 or the `.devcontainer` (`STUDENTS.md` §6).
- `tests/integration` and `tests/e2e` share one Gitea instance per run, so a test that leaves state
  behind breaks later tests rather than itself.
- `loginUser` cannot get past the TOTP step, so it never signs in a user who has 2FA. Sign in first,
  then insert the `TwoFactor` row (`tests/integration/org_two_factor_test.go`); the session stays valid.
- `unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &Foo{ID: 1, Bar: x})` turns the bean into the `WHERE`, and
  XORM leaves out zero-valued and `xorm:"-"` fields, so those are never checked. To verify a stored
  value, load by ID and compare fields (`models/issues/issue_close_reason_test.go`).

## Related

- `architecture.md` — which layer the code under test belongs to
- `docs/testing.md` — full documentation, including non-SQLite database setup

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `routers/web/web.go` | `Routes`, `registerWebRoutes`, `verifyAuthWithOptions` |
| `routers/web/repo/issue.go` | a representative handler set, and the `templates.TplName` constants |
| `routers/common/pagetmpl.go` | `PageGlobalData` — data every template can rely on |
| `routers/common/middleware.go` | `MustInitSessioner` |
| `routers/common/blockexpensive.go`, `qos.go` | `BlockExpensive`, `QoS` load shedding |
| `routers/common/errpage.go` | the panic/error page renderer |
| `modules/web/router.go` | `Bind`, `GetForm` |
| `services/context/context_response.go` | `HTML`, and the dev-only `ctx.Data["TemplateName"]` |
| `templates/base/footer_content.tmpl` | prints that template name in the page footer |

## Conventions & invariants

- A handler is `func Foo(ctx *context.Context)` from `gitea.dev/services/context`. It puts data in
  `ctx.Data`, then calls `ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplFoo)`.
- Not every handler renders a template: one backing a JS-driven widget on an otherwise-HTML page
  calls `ctx.JSON` instead, e.g. `routers/web/repo/issue_suggestions.go`. That stays in
  `routers/web`, distinct from the `/api/v1` JSON layer (`routers-api-v1.md`).
- `tplFoo` is a package-level `templates.TplName` constant whose value is a path under `templates/`
  without the extension — `tplIssues templates.TplName = "repo/issue/list"`.
- `ctx.Data` is the only channel from handler to template. A template cannot reach anything the
  handler did not put there.
- Sign-in guards are local variables built at the top of `registerWebRoutes` from
  `verifyAuthWithOptions`: `reqSignIn`, `reqSignOut`, `optSignIn`, `optExploreSignIn`. A new guard
  is declared there too, not in a subpackage.
- Repo pages get `context.RepoAssignment` (see `services-context.md`), which fills `ctx.Repo`;
  ref-scoped pages add `context.RepoRefByType`.
- A POST that takes a form is registered as
  `m.Post("/path", web.Bind(forms.XxxForm{}), handler)`; the handler reads it back with
  `web.GetForm(ctx)`.
- The middleware chain in `Routes` is, in order: `chi_middleware.GetHead`, optional gzip,
  `common.MustInitSessioner`, `context.Contexter`, the web auth middleware, `goGet`,
  `common.PageGlobalData`, then `common.BlockExpensive` and `common.QoS`.

## Recipes

**Add a page.**

1. Handler in the matching `routers/web/<area>/` file, signature `func(ctx *context.Context)`.
2. A `templates.TplName` constant beside the other constants in that file.
3. The template file at the matching path under `templates/`.
4. The route inside the right `m.Group` in `registerWebRoutes`, with the guards that group needs.
5. Any user-visible string as a key in `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` — never a literal.

**Add a form POST.** Do the above, plus a form struct in `services/forms/` and `web.Bind` on the
route. See `services-forms-and-convert.md`.

**Find the template behind a page you are looking at.** Outside production, `ctx.HTML` sets
`ctx.Data["TemplateName"]` and `templates/base/footer_content.tmpl` prints it in the page footer, so
a dev instance names its own template on every page. Failing that, grep the visible string in
`options/locale/locale_en-US.json` for its key, then grep that key under `templates/`. To go the
other way, from a template to its handler, grep for the `TplName` value — the template path without
the extension.

## Gotchas

- The static routes registered on `routes` *before* the `mid` slice is assembled (`/assets/*`,
  `/avatars/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/api/healthz`) deliberately bypass session and auth middleware.
  Do not add an authenticated route there.
- `registerWebRoutes` is long. Find your group by URL prefix rather than reading top to bottom, and
  add the route to the group that already carries the guards you need instead of re-listing them.
- `ctx.HTML` after something has already written the response is a bug; `ctx.Written()` reports
  whether that happened.
- The issue page loads each comment type's linked data in one `if … else if` chain over
  `issue.Comments` (`routers/web/repo/issue_view.go`). A new type's loading goes there as its own
  branch; a type matched by an earlier branch never reaches a later one. That chain is also where
  linked data the viewer may not see is dropped: a close comment's duplicate target is cleared
  unless `ctx.Repo.Permission.CanReadIssuesOrPulls` allows its kind, so templates never show it.
- A handler branch that only logs an error still redirects as if it worked. `NewComment`
  (`routers/web/repo/issue_comment.go`) shows a flash only for the close refusals it maps, so every
  refusal a person can cause needs its own `ctx.Flash.Error(ctx.Tr(...))`.
```

**Merging and closing judge dependencies differently.** The merge button, the API and a scheduled
merge all go through `CheckPullMergeable`, which asks `MergeBlockedByDependencies`: does
this pull request still depend on an open issue, or on a pull request that was never merged?
Closing asks a looser question, through `IssueNoDependenciesLeft`: is everything it depends on
closed? So a dependency that was closed without merging blocks a merge but not a close. When a
repository turns dependencies off in its settings, the merge check skips them, as closing already
does. The two rules live apart, so changing one leaves the other as it was.

**Write a migration test.** Put it next to the migration in `models/migrations/`, with its own
fixtures under `models/migrations/fixtures/` and helpers from `models/migrations/migrationtest/`.

## Traps, and what they look like

**A database test fails with something about a nil or closed connection.** The package is missing
its `main_test.go`, so no test database was ever built.

**Your test passes alone and fails in the full run.** Either it is missing
`unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()`, or an earlier test left state behind. Integration and browser
tests share one Gitea instance for the whole run, so a test that creates something and does not
clean up breaks a *later* test, not itself — the failure points at innocent code.

**`CheckConsistencyFor` fails in a test you did not write.** You added or changed a fixture row and
a counter column no longer matches.

**Your assertion passes even though the value was never saved.** `unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean`
finds a row by turning the struct you pass into the SQL `WHERE`, and it silently drops zero values
and fields tagged `xorm:"-"`. So asking for `{ID: 1, Bar: 0}` checks only the ID. Load the row by
ID, then compare its fields, as `models/issues/issue_close_reason_test.go` does.

**Your test user with 2FA is never actually signed in.** `loginUser` stops at the code-entry step,
so the user is left signed out. Sign them in first, then add their `TwoFactor` row; the session
keeps working (`tests/integration/org_two_factor_test.go`).

**A browser test only passes when you raise `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR`.** That multiplier
defaults to 4 on CI and 1 locally. Needing more is a flaky test — usually waiting on the wrong
thing — not a slow laptop. Fix the wait, do not raise the number.

**A handful of Go tests fail on Windows** for symlink and temp-file reasons that are not your bug.
Run the suite on Linux, macOS, WSL2 or the provided `.devcontainer`.

**You cannot tell what a failing database test actually did.** Set `GITEA_TEST_LOG_SQL=1` and it
prints every SQL statement it ran. This is the fastest debugging tool here.

**A dependency you added in a test blocks nothing.** The fixture repositories never switch
dependencies on, so they count as off. Turn them on first with `repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig`,
as `tests/integration/pull_merge_dependency_test.go` does.

## Where to go next

- `docs/testing.md` (in this folder) — the reference page this was written from
- Gitea's own `docs/testing.md`, at the repository root — the project's full test documentation,
  including how to run against a database other than SQLite. Same filename, different file:
  everything in `.claude-students/` is ours, everything at the repository root is Gitea's.
- `architecture.md` — which layer the code you are testing belongs to

  - The buttons are drawn by the Vue form.
  - A blocker nobody may override has to remove the merge styles. Adding it to the overridable blockers would keep the buttons for anyone who can bypass branch protection.

  It took several files to work out, which passes rule 3's test for what gets recorded.
