=== .gitar/review/course.md
# Reviewing this repository

This repository is a CSCI 435 course fork of Gitea. Pull requests are graded against the course
rules as well as Gitea's own conventions, so review against both. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are
read already; these are the course and project rules they point to:

@.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md
@.claude-students/AI-ASSISTANCE.md
@CONTRIBUTING.md
@docs/sprint0/standards.md

## Focus on

- Whether the change does what the linked issue's acceptance criteria ask, and nothing outside its
  scope.
- Whether each test checks real behaviour and can fail: no assertion that passes for an unrelated
  reason, no "nothing happened" check without waiting, no test that depends on fixture data by
  chance.
- Bugs and security problems, with the input or state that triggers them.

## Leave alone

- The pull request description's sections and format: CodeRabbit checks those.
- The pull request title's Conventional Commit format: the `pr-title` CI job checks it.
- Formatting and anything else the repository's linters already enforce (`make lint`).
- Style preferences that no rule above asks for. These are students learning a large codebase;
  one clear finding helps more than several small ones.
=== .gitar/rules/commit-messages.md
---
title: "Commit messages follow AGENTS.md"
description: "Each commit subject is a Conventional Commit, ends with the issue number when the PR closes an issue, and credits AI with an Assisted-by trailer rather than Co-Authored-By"
type: check
when: "Every pull request"
actions: "Post a comment listing each commit that breaks a rule below, and which rule"
---

# Commit messages

From `AGENTS.md`. Check every commit in the pull request except merge commits (subjects starting
with `Merge`).

1. The subject is a Conventional Commit, `type(scope): subject`, with `!` before the colon for a
   breaking change. A commit that only changes tests uses the `test` type.
2. When the pull request closes an issue (`Closes #123`), the subject ends with that issue's number,
   for example `(#123)`. Chore pull requests that close no issue are exempt.
3. AI help is credited with a trailer in the form `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION`, for
   example `Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5`, never with a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer that
   names an AI tool or model.

A `Signed-off-by:` trailer is not judged: signing off is the human author's own step.
=== .gitar/rules/skipped-tests-need-an-issue.md
---
title: "Skipped tests and disabled checks link an issue"
description: "A test that is skipped or expected to fail, or a CI check that is turned off, needs a linked issue and a code comment giving the reason"
type: check
when: "PRs that add or change a skipped test, a test expected to fail, or a disabled CI job, step or check"
actions: "Post a comment naming each skip or disabled check that has no linked issue or no reason in a code comment"
---

# Skipped tests and disabled checks

The course and `AGENTS.md` say: never skip a test or disable a CI check without a linked issue and
a code comment giving the reason.

Count only what this pull request adds or changes:

- Go: `t.Skip`, `t.Skipf`, `t.SkipNow`.
- Vitest and Playwright: `test.skip`, `it.skip`, `describe.skip`, `test.fixme`, `test.fail`, and
  the same through `.skipIf` or `.runIf`.
- Workflows under `.github/workflows/`: a job or step that runs tests or a check and is turned off
  (`if: false`), removed, or allowed to fail (`continue-on-error: true`).

Each one is met when a comment next to it gives the reason and names an issue (`#123` or a link to
it). Skips that already existed and that the pull request does not touch are not counted.
=== .gitar/rules/test-expected-values.md
---
title: "Test expected values come from a source"
description: "Every expected value in a new or changed test can be traced to the source its Test Evidence row names, not to the code's current output"
type: check
when: "PRs that add or change tests (*_test.go, *.test.ts, or files under tests/)"
actions: "Post a comment naming each expected value whose source cannot be found, and what the description cites for it"
---

# Expected values in tests

The course's Test Evidence rule (`.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`): an expected value comes
from the acceptance criteria, the issue discussion, docs or upstream behaviour, never from the
current output of the code under test. A test that copies the code's output cannot catch the code
being wrong.

For each assertion the pull request adds or changes (`assert`/`require` in Go, `expect` in Vitest
and Playwright), find the matching row of the description's "Test Evidence" table and its "Source of
expected value". The value is met when it appears in, or follows directly from, that source: the
linked issue's acceptance criteria or discussion, quoted docs, or the behaviour the row says it
keeps.

Flag only clear cases:

- a value that the cited source does not contain and the row does not explain under "other";
- a snapshot or golden file that was regenerated with no source given;
- a value that only repeats a constant or string from the code under test.

Setup values such as fixture IDs, user names and timeouts are not expected values.
```
</details></tool-use>

Show which dependencies block a pull request from merging, and whether each is open, merged or closed

> Blocked by #143, which decides which dependencies block a merge.

## User Story

As a maintainer about to merge a pull request, I want its page to tell me which dependencies still block it, and whether each one is open, merged or closed, so that I know why it cannot be merged before I press Merge, not after.

## User Scenario
Sam's pull request #12 depends on pull request #11, which was closed without merging, and on issue #9, which is still open. When a maintainer opens #12, the merge box, where blockers such as missing approvals already appear, says "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:" followed by links to #11 and #9 with their titles. No merge button is offered.

In the sidebar, the "Depends on" list shows each entry's state: #11 "Closed", #9 "Open". Today both just look closed or open, and a merged pull request looks the same as a closed one. Once #9 is closed and #11 is reopened and merged, the merge box shows the merge button again.

| Dependency | Sidebar shows | Blocks merging (#143) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open issue or pull request | Open | Yes |
| Closed issue | Closed | No |
| Merged pull request | Merged | No |
| Pull request closed without merging | Closed | Yes |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a pull request with a dependency that blocks merging, when it is opened, then its merge box shows "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:" followed by a link to each blocking dependency, shown as in the timeline: #N title for one in the same repository, owner/repo#N - title for one in another repository.
- [ ] AC2: Given the same, when a user with merge rights opens it, then no merge button is offered, including its "(When checks succeed)" form; "Manually merged" stays offered where the repository allows it, as #143 leaves it unblocked.
- [ ] AC3: Given a pull request with no dependencies, or whose dependencies are all resolved, when it is opened, then the merge box looks as it does today.
- [ ] AC4: Given a blocking dependency the viewer cannot read, when they open the pull request, then the merge box counts it as "You do not have permission to read 1 dependency" without its title, as the sidebar does today.
- [ ] AC5: Given the "Depends on" or "Blocks" list in the sidebar of an issue or pull request, when it is shown, then each entry shows its state: "Open", "Closed", or "Merged" for a merged pull request.
- [ ] AC6: Given a repository with "Enable Dependencies For Issues and Pull Requests" turned off, when a pull request is opened, then neither the merge box nor the sidebar shows dependencies, as the sidebar does today.

## Out of Scope
- Which dependencies block a merge, and refusing the merge: Issue (#143)
- Showing dependencies on the issue and pull request lists.
- Changing how dependencies are added or removed.

## Open Questions
None

## Design Decisions
Added per commit during implementation, as in #53 and #54.

## Scope
medium (3 points). Touches two parts of the pull request page, the merge box and the sidebar's dependency lists, plus one new message; moderate changes to the page's data and templates, with browser tests for both parts.

## AI Disclosure
Used claude-code for the drafting of this issue, followed by my changes and proofing. Changes after the spec review were also made with claude-code.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Test evidence — does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally? | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
```

## Mutation testing (D6)

A mutation testing tool makes small changes to the code (*mutants*), such as flipping a condition
or a boundary value, and runs the tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is
**killed**. If every test passes, it **survived**: the tests didn't notice the change, which points
to a weak or missing test. An **equivalent** mutant behaves exactly like the original code, so no
test can kill it. Definitions are in the course Glossary.

**Which issue:** one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests (CSCI 535: two, and the
small issue may be one of them). A tool is required; mutating code by hand doesn't count.

| Code changed | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend TypeScript (Vitest) | StrykerJS with the Vitest runner |
| Go backend | Gremlins or go-mutesting |

1. Run the tool on the **source files changed by your PR(s)** for that issue, not the whole
   project.
2. Analyse every surviving mutant: equivalent, or a gap in your tests? If more than 10 survive,
   analyse at least 10, starting with lines your PR added or changed.
3. Add or strengthen **at least one test that kills a survivor** that revealed a gap, and re-run
   the tool to confirm it is killed. If no survivor reveals a gap (all killed or equivalent), say so
   and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
4. Answer the three questions in the write-up.

Files:

- Write-up: `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<github-username>.md`, using the template below.
- Reports: machine-readable output of the first run and the re-run, as
  `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<github-username>-before.json` and `-after.json` (`.txt`
  for go-mutesting). StrykerJS: add `"json"` to `reporters`. Gremlins: `--output=<file>.json`.
  go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file. The scores in the write-up must match the
  reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.
- The tool configuration you used, committed and linked from the write-up. Reusing a teammate's
  setup is encouraged, as long as you run the tool yourself and credit them. The team's shared
  setup (go-mutesting for Go), its commands and its pitfalls: `.claude-students/docs/mutation-testing.md`.

Common problems:

- **The tool stops before mutating.** It first runs the selected tests on unchanged code and stops
  if any fail. Fix or exclude them first; the D8 baseline shows which ones fail already.
- **Tests run against built code.** Mutants in the source are never seen by tests that run on
  compiled output. Configure a rebuild, or pick tests that run on source.
- **Tests need services.** Start the database or service first. How each test type runs is in
  `.claude-students/docs/testing.md`.
- **False survivors.** When limiting which tests run, include the tests that cover the mutated
  files. Otherwise mutants they would catch show as survived or not covered. Check that the
  relevant tests ran before writing a new test for a survivor.
- **Blocked?** Ask teammates first. Then tell the TA **as early as possible**, with the errors and
  the AI log of what you tried; the TA may approve a different issue or area. Problems reported at
  the end of the sprint don't excuse a missing D6.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a pull request with a dependency that blocks merging, when it is opened, then its merge box shows "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:" followed by a link to each blocking dependency, shown as in the timeline: #N title for one in the same repository, owner/repo#N - title for one in another repository.
- [ ] AC2: Given the same, when a user with merge rights opens it, then no merge button is offered, including its "(When checks succeed)" form; "Manually merged" stays offered where the repository allows it, as #143 leaves it unblocked.
- [ ] AC3: Given a pull request with no dependencies, or whose dependencies are all resolved, when it is opened, then the merge box looks as it does today.
- [ ] AC4: Given a blocking dependency the viewer cannot read, when they open the pull request, then the merge box counts it as "You do not have permission to read 1 dependency" without its title, as the sidebar does today.
- [ ] AC5: Given the "Depends on" or "Blocks" list in the sidebar of an issue or pull request, when it is shown, then each entry shows its state: "Open", "Closed", or "Merged" for a merged pull request.
- [ ] AC6: Given a repository with "Enable Dependencies For Issues and Pull Requests" turned off, when a pull request is opened, then neither the merge box nor the sidebar shows dependencies, as the sidebar does today.

## Out of Scope
- Which dependencies block a merge, and refusing the merge: Issue (#143)
- Showing dependencies on the issue and pull request lists.
- Changing how dependencies are added or removed.

## Open Questions
None

## Design Decisions
Added per commit during implementation, as in #53 and #54.

## Scope
medium (3 points). Touches two parts of the pull request page, the merge box and the sidebar's dependency lists, plus one new message; moderate changes to the page's data and templates, with browser tests for both parts.

+// GetMergeBlockingDependencies returns the dependencies that block merging pr, each with its repository loaded.
+func GetMergeBlockingDependencies(ctx context.Context, pr *PullRequest) (issueDeps []*DependencyInfo, err error) {
+	err = db.GetEngine(ctx).
+		Table("issue").
+		Join("INNER", "repository", "repository.id = issue.repo_id").
+		Join("INNER", "issue_dependency", "issue_dependency.dependency_id = issue.id").
+		Where("issue_dependency.issue_id = ?", pr.IssueID).
+		And(mergeBlockingDependencyCond()).
+		Find(&issueDeps)
+
+	for _, depInfo := range issueDeps {
+		depInfo.Issue.Repo = &depInfo.Repository
+	}
+
+	return issueDeps, err
+}
+
+// mergeBlockingDependencyCond matches an open issue or pull request, or a pull request closed without merging.
+// Shared so the merge check and the merge box list the same dependencies.
+func mergeBlockingDependencyCond() builder.Cond {
+	return builder.Or(
+		builder.Eq{"issue.is_closed": false},
+		builder.In("issue.id", builder.Select("issue_id").From("pull_request").Where(builder.Eq{"has_merged": false})),
+	)
+}

+	deps, err := issues_model.GetMergeBlockingDependencies(ctx, prInfo.issue.PullRequest)

+	}

+	doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 1})
+	pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2}) // issue 3, repo 1

+
+	// one dependency of each kind in the issue's table, closed first where needed

+		issueID int64
+		close   bool
+	}{
+		{1, false},  // open issue
+		{5, false},  // closed issue, closed in the fixtures
+		{2, true},   // merged pull request 1; closed as a real merge would, the fixture leaves it open
+		{11, true},  // pull request 5, closed without merging
+		{12, false}, // open pull request 6, in repo 3
+	} {

+// prepareMergeBoxDependencies lists the dependencies that block merging, the same ones the merge check refuses.
+func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) prepareMergeBoxDependencies(ctx *context.Context) {
+	if !ctx.Repo.Repository.IsDependenciesEnabled(ctx) {
+		return
+	}
+	deps, err := issues_model.GetMergeBlockingDependencies(ctx, prInfo.issue.PullRequest)
+	if err != nil {
+		ctx.ServerError("GetMergeBlockingDependencies", err)
+		return
+	}
+	if len(deps) == 0 {
+		return
+	}
+	prInfo.MergeBoxData.isBlockedByDependencies = true
+	canRead, notPermitted := checkBlockedByIssues(ctx, deps)
+	if ctx.Written() {
+		return
+	}
+
+	items := make([]template.HTML, 0, len(canRead)+1)
+	for _, dep := range canRead {
+		// as the timeline shows a dependency: the repository only when it is another one
+		if dep.Issue.RepoID == prInfo.issue.RepoID {
+			items = append(items, htmlutil.HTMLFormat(`<a href="%s">#%d %s</a>`, dep.Issue.Link(), dep.Issue.Index, dep.Issue.Title))
+		} else {
+			items = append(items, htmlutil.HTMLFormat(`<a href="%s">%s#%d - %s</a>`, dep.Issue.Link(), dep.Issue.Repo.FullName(), dep.Issue.Index, dep.Issue.Title))
+		}
+	}
+	if len(notPermitted) > 0 {
+		items = append(items, ctx.Locale.TrN(len(notPermitted), "repo.issues.dependency.no_permission_1", "repo.issues.dependency.no_permission_n", len(notPermitted)))
+	}
+	prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddErrorItem(ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.blocked_by_dependencies"), items)
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,165 @@
+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package repo
+
+import (
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
+	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
+	"gitea.dev/models/unit"
+	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
+	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/translation"
+	"gitea.dev/services/context"
+	"gitea.dev/services/contexttest"
+
+	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+// mockPullWithDependencies opens pull request 2 (issue 3 in user2/repo1) as viewerID, after user2 gives it the dependencies depIDs.
+// It loads the real English locale, as the expected texts are the English ones.
+func mockPullWithDependencies(t *testing.T, viewerID int64, dependenciesEnabled bool, depIDs ...int64) (*context.Context, *pullRequestViewInfo) {
+	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
+	translation.InitLocales(t.Context())
+	owner := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
+	pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2})
+	require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
+	for _, depID := range depIDs {
+		dep := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: depID})
+		require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(t.Context(), owner, pr.Issue, dep))
+	}
+	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
+	issuesUnit, err := repo.GetUnit(t.Context(), unit.TypeIssues)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	issuesUnit.IssuesConfig().EnableDependencies = dependenciesEnabled // fixture repos leave it unset, which reads as off
+	require.NoError(t, repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig(t.Context(), issuesUnit))
+
+	ctx, _ := contexttest.MockContext(t, "user2/repo1/pulls/2")
+	ctx.Locale = translation.NewLocale("en-US")
+	contexttest.LoadUser(t, ctx, viewerID)
+	contexttest.LoadRepo(t, ctx, 1)
+	return ctx, &pullRequestViewInfo{issue: pr.Issue, MergeBoxData: &pullMergeBoxData{}}
+}
+
+func TestPrepareMergeBoxDependencies(t *testing.T) {
+	// the merge box's blockers as text: each message, then each of its list entries as "text -> link"
+	blockers := func(t *testing.T, viewerID int64, dependenciesEnabled bool, depIDs ...int64) []string {
+		ctx, prInfo := mockPullWithDependencies(t, viewerID, dependenciesEnabled, depIDs...)
+		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxDependencies(ctx)
+		require.False(t, ctx.Written())
+
+		texts := []string{}
+		for _, item := range prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.items {
+			texts = append(texts, string(item.InfoHTML))
+			for _, listItem := range item.ListItems {
+				doc, err := goquery.NewDocumentFromReader(strings.NewReader(string(listItem)))
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				text := strings.TrimSpace(doc.Text())
+				if href, ok := doc.Find("a").Attr("href"); ok {
+					text += " -> " + href
+				}
+				texts = append(texts, text)
+			}
+		}
+		return texts
+	}
+
+	t.Run("AC1 links each blocking dependency", func(t *testing.T) {
+		// issue 1 (#1) is in the same repository, issue 7 (#2) in user2/repo2
+		texts := blockers(t, 2, true, 1, 7)
+		require.NotEmpty(t, texts)
+		assert.Equal(t, "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:", texts[0])
+		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
+			"#1 issue1 -> /user2/repo1/issues/1",
+			"user2/repo2#2 - issue7 -> /user2/repo2/issues/2",
+		}, texts[1:])
+	})
+	t.Run("AC3 no dependencies", func(t *testing.T) {
+		assert.Empty(t, blockers(t, 2, true))
+	})
+	t.Run("AC4 counts a dependency the viewer cannot read", func(t *testing.T) {
+		// user4 can read the public user2/repo1 but not the private user2/repo2
+		texts := blockers(t, 4, true, 1, 7)
+		require.NotEmpty(t, texts)
+		assert.Equal(t, "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:", texts[0])
+		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
+			"#1 issue1 -> /user2/repo1/issues/1",
+			"You do not have permission to read 1 dependency",
+		}, texts[1:])
+	})
+	t.Run("AC6 dependencies turned off", func(t *testing.T) {
+		assert.Empty(t, blockers(t, 2, false, 1, 7))
+	})
+}
+
+func TestPrepareMergeBoxFormWithDependencies(t *testing.T) {
+	type offer struct {
+		styles   []string // the merge styles offered, "+auto" where "(When checks succeed)" is offered with it; nil when there is no merge form
+		messages []string
+	}
+	// user2 owns user2/repo1 and may merge pull request 2, whose branch merges cleanly. checksPending holds the merge back
+	// for status checks user2 cannot bypass, which is when "(When checks succeed)" is offered.
+	mergeBox := func(t *testing.T, allowManualMerge, checksPending bool, depIDs ...int64) offer {
+		ctx, prInfo := mockPullWithDependencies(t, 2, true, depIDs...)
+		contexttest.LoadGitRepo(t, ctx)
+		defer ctx.Repo.GitRepo.Close()
+		ctx.Repo.Repository.MustGetUnit(ctx, unit.TypePullRequests).PullRequestsConfig().AllowManualMerge = allowManualMerge
+		data := prInfo.MergeBoxData
+		data.hasPermToMerge = true
+		data.hasOverridableBlockers = checksPending
+		data.canMergeNow = !checksPending
+
+		// in the order prepareMergeBox runs them
+		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxDependencies(ctx)
+		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxFormProps(ctx)
+		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxInfoItems(ctx)
+		require.False(t, ctx.Written())
+
+		var o offer
+		if data.MergeFormProps != nil {
+			for _, s := range data.MergeFormProps["mergeStyles"].([]any) {
+				style := s.(map[string]any)
+				if !style["allowed"].(bool) {
+					continue
+				}
+				name := style["name"].(string)
+				if !style["hideAutoMerge"].(bool) {
+					name += "+auto"
+				}
+				o.styles = append(o.styles, name)
+			}
+		}
+		for _, section := range data.InfoSections {
+			for _, item := range section.InfoItems {
+				o.messages = append(o.messages, string(item.InfoHTML))
+			}
+		}
+		return o
+	}
+
+	t.Run("AC2 only Manually merged while blocked", func(t *testing.T) {
+		o := mergeBox(t, true, false, 1)
+		assert.Equal(t, []string{"manually-merged"}, o.styles)
+		assert.NotContains(t, o.messages, "This pull request can be merged automatically.")
+	})
+	t.Run("AC2 no merge form while blocked and waiting for checks", func(t *testing.T) {
+		o := mergeBox(t, false, true, 1)
+		assert.Nil(t, o.styles)
+		assert.NotContains(t, o.messages, "This pull request cannot be merged because all repository merge options are disabled.")
+	})
+	t.Run("control: waiting for checks offers (When checks succeed)", func(t *testing.T) {
+		assert.Contains(t, mergeBox(t, false, true).styles, "merge+auto")
+	})
+	t.Run("AC3 resolved dependencies look as with none", func(t *testing.T) {
+		none := mergeBox(t, false, false)
+		// the styles user2/repo1 allows: four in its fixture, plus fast-forward-only, which is on by default
+		assert.Equal(t, []string{"merge", "rebase", "rebase-merge", "squash", "fast-forward-only"}, none.styles)
+		assert.Contains(t, none.messages, "This pull request can be merged automatically.")
+		assert.Equal(t, none, mergeBox(t, false, false, 5)) // issue 5 is closed
+	})
+}

diff --git a/tests/e2e/issue-dependencies.test.ts b/tests/e2e/issue-dependencies.test.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..33dcc532cc
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/e2e/issue-dependencies.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+import {env} from 'node:process';
+import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
+import type {APIRequestContext} from '@playwright/test';
+import {apiCreateFile, apiCreateIssue, apiCreatePR, apiCreateRepo, apiEditRepo, apiHeaders, baseUrl, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';
+
+const owner = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;
+
+// a repository whose issues can have dependencies, set here rather than left to the server's default
+async function createRepoWithDependencies(request: APIRequestContext, name: string, extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}) {
+  await apiCreateRepo(request, {name});
+  await apiEditRepo(request, owner, name, {
+    has_issues: true, // the API ignores internal_tracker without it
+    internal_tracker: {enable_time_tracker: true, allow_only_contributors_to_track_time: true, enable_issue_dependencies: true},
+    ...extra,
+  });
+}
+
+async function createPull(request: APIRequestContext, repo: string, branch: string, title: string) {
+  await apiCreateFile(request, owner, repo, `${branch}.txt`, `${branch}\n`, {newBranch: branch});
+  return apiCreatePR(request, owner, repo, branch, 'main', title);
+}
+
+async function addDependency(request: APIRequestContext, repo: string, index: number, dependsOn: number) {
+  const response = await request.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${index}/dependencies`, {
+    headers: apiHeaders(),
+    data: {owner, repo, index: dependsOn},
+  });
+  expect(response.ok()).toBeTruthy();
+}
+
+test('#144 AC1 AC2 the merge box names the blocking dependency and offers only Manually merged', async ({page, request}) => {
+  const repo = `e2e-merge-deps-${randomString(8)}`;
+  await createRepoWithDependencies(request, repo, {allow_manual_merge: true});
+  const pull = await createPull(request, repo, 'blocked', 'Blocked pull');
+  const {index: issue} = await apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo, title: 'Open dependency'});
+  await Promise.all([addDependency(request, repo, pull, issue), login(page)]);
+
+  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repo}/pulls/${pull}`);
+  const mergeBox = page.locator('.pull-merge-box');
+  await expect(mergeBox.getByText('This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:')).toBeVisible();
+  await expect(mergeBox.getByRole('link', {name: `#${issue} Open dependency`})).toHaveAttribute('href', `/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${issue}`);
+
+  // wait for the merge form to load before checking what it offers, so an empty form cannot pass
+  await expect(mergeBox.getByRole('button', {name: 'Manually merged'})).toBeVisible();
+  await mergeBox.locator('.merge-button .dropdown').click();
+  await expect(mergeBox.locator('.merge-button .menu .item')).toHaveText(['Manually merged']); // no other style, no "(When checks succeed)"
+});
+
+test('#144 AC5 the sidebar shows each dependency as Open, Closed or Merged', async ({page, request}) => {
+  const repo = `e2e-dep-states-${randomString(8)}`;
+  await createRepoWithDependencies(request, repo);
+  const {index: subject} = await apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo, title: 'Subject'});
+  const [{index: open}, closed, merged] = await Promise.all([
+    apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo, title: 'Open issue'}),
+    createPull(request, repo, 'closed', 'Closed pull'),
+    createPull(request, repo, 'merged', 'Merged pull'),
+  ]);
+  const pulls = `${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/pulls`;
+  expect((await request.patch(`${pulls}/${closed}`, {headers: apiHeaders(), data: {state: 'closed'}})).ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  await expect(async () => { // the merge is refused until the new pull request's conflict check has finished
+    expect((await request.post(`${pulls}/${merged}/merge`, {headers: apiHeaders(), data: {Do: 'merge'}})).ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  }).toPass();
+  await Promise.all([
+    ...[open, closed, merged].map((dep) => addDependency(request, repo, subject, dep)),
+    login(page),
+  ]);
+
+  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${subject}`);
+  const entries = page.locator('.ui.depending .item.dependency');
+  await expect(entries.filter({hasText: `#${open} Open issue`})).toContainText('· Open');
+  await expect(entries.filter({hasText: `#${closed} Closed pull`})).toContainText('· Closed');
+  await expect(entries.filter({hasText: `#${merged} Merged pull`})).toContainText('· Merged');
+});

package repo

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"

func TestIssueViewSidebarDependencyStates(t *testing.T) {
	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
	translation.InitLocales(t.Context()) // the expected texts are the English ones
	owner := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	issuesUnit, err := repo.GetUnit(t.Context(), unit.TypeIssues)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	issuesUnit.IssuesConfig().EnableDependencies = true // fixture repos leave it unset, which reads as off
	require.NoError(t, repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig(t.Context(), issuesUnit))

	// in user2/repo1: issue 1 (#1) open, issue 2 (#2) merged pull request 1, issue 3 (#3) open pull request 2,
	// issue 5 (#4) closed in the fixtures, issue 11 (#5) pull request 5 closed without merging; issue 7 is #2 in the private user2/repo2
	for _, id := range []int64{2, 11} { // pull request 1 is merged but the fixture leaves it open, so close it as a real merge would
		_, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: id}), owner, issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{})
		require.NoError(t, err)
	}
	for _, dep := range [][2]int64{{3, 1}, {3, 2}, {3, 5}, {3, 11}, {3, 7}, {2, 1}, {5, 1}, {11, 1}} { // {issue, the issue it depends on}
		issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: dep[0]})
		require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(t.Context(), owner, issue, unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: dep[1]})))
	}

	// the entries of one sidebar list ("Depends on" or "Blocks") on issueID's page, as viewerID reads them
	sidebarList := func(t *testing.T, viewerID, issueID int64, heading string) []string {
		ctx, resp := contexttest.MockContext(t, "/", contexttest.MockContextOption{Render: templates.PageRenderer()})
		ctx.Locale = translation.NewLocale("en-US")
		ctx.TemplateContext["Locale"] = ctx.Locale // templates read the locale the context was created with
		contexttest.LoadUser(t, ctx, viewerID)
		contexttest.LoadRepo(t, ctx, 1)
		issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: issueID})
		require.NoError(t, issue.LoadRepo(ctx))
		ctx.Data["Issue"] = issue
		ctx.Data["Repository"] = ctx.Repo.Repository

		prepareIssueViewSidebarDependency(ctx, issue)
		require.False(t, ctx.Written())
		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, "repo/issue/sidebar/issue_dependencies")

		doc, err := goquery.NewDocumentFromReader(resp.Body)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		entries := []string{}
		doc.Find("strong").FilterFunction(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) bool { return s.Text() == heading }).
			Parent().Next().Find(".item").Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
			// tests render each icon as its name in a span; AC5 asks for the state word, so leave the icons out
			s.Find("span").FilterFunction(func(_ int, e *goquery.Selection) bool {
				return e.Children().Length() == 0 && strings.HasPrefix(e.Text(), "octicon-")
			}).Remove()
			entries = append(entries, strings.Join(strings.Fields(s.Text()), " "))
		})
		return entries
	}

	t.Run("AC5 Depends on", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
			"#1 issue1 user2/repo1 · Open",
			"#2 issue2 user2/repo1 · Merged",
			"#4 issue5 user2/repo1 · Closed",
			"#5 pull5 user2/repo1 · Closed",
			"#2 issue7 user2/repo2 · Open",
		}, sidebarList(t, 2, 3, "Depends on"))
	})
	t.Run("AC5 Blocks", func(t *testing.T) {
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
			"#3 issue3 user2/repo1 · Open",
			"#2 issue2 user2/repo1 · Merged",
			"#4 issue5 user2/repo1 · Closed",
			"#5 pull5 user2/repo1 · Closed",
		}, sidebarList(t, 2, 1, "Blocks"))
	})
	t.Run("AC5 an entry the viewer can remove but not read", func(t *testing.T) {
		// user40 may write to user2/repo1, so it manages dependencies, but cannot read user2/repo2
		assert.Contains(t, sidebarList(t, 40, 3, "Depends on"), "#2 issue7 user2/repo2 · Open")
	})
}

Show which dependencies block a pull request from merging, and whether each is open, merged or closed

> Blocked by #143, which decides which dependencies block a merge.

## User Story

As a maintainer about to merge a pull request, I want its page to tell me which dependencies still block it, and whether each one is open, merged or closed, so that I know why it cannot be merged before I press Merge, not after.

## User Scenario
Sam's pull request #12 depends on pull request #11, which was closed without merging, and on issue #9, which is still open. When a maintainer opens #12, the merge box, where blockers such as missing approvals already appear, says "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:" followed by links to #11 and #9 with their titles. No merge button is offered.

In the sidebar, the "Depends on" list shows each entry's state: #11 "Closed", #9 "Open". Today both just look closed or open, and a merged pull request looks the same as a closed one. Once #9 is closed and #11 is reopened and merged, the merge box shows the merge button again.

| Dependency | Sidebar shows | Blocks merging (#143) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open issue or pull request | Open | Yes |
| Closed issue | Closed | No |
| Merged pull request | Merged | No |
| Pull request closed without merging | Closed | Yes |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a pull request with a dependency that blocks merging, when it is opened, then its merge box shows "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:" followed by a link to each blocking dependency, shown as in the timeline: #N title for one in the same repository, owner/repo#N - title for one in another repository.
- [ ] AC2: Given the same, when a user with merge rights opens it, then no merge button is offered, including its "(When checks succeed)" form; "Manually merged" stays offered where the repository allows it, as #143 leaves it unblocked.
- [ ] AC3: Given a pull request with no dependencies, or whose dependencies are all resolved, when it is opened, then the merge box looks as it does today.
- [ ] AC4: Given a blocking dependency the viewer cannot read, when they open the pull request, then the merge box counts it as "You do not have permission to read 1 dependency" without its title, as the sidebar does today.
- [ ] AC5: Given the "Depends on" or "Blocks" list in the sidebar of an issue or pull request, when it is shown, then each entry shows its state: "Open", "Closed", or "Merged" for a merged pull request.
- [ ] AC6: Given a repository with "Enable Dependencies For Issues and Pull Requests" turned off, when a pull request is opened, then neither the merge box nor the sidebar shows dependencies, as the sidebar does today.

## Out of Scope
- Which dependencies block a merge, and refusing the merge: Issue (#143)
- Showing dependencies on the issue and pull request lists.
- Changing how dependencies are added or removed.

## Open Questions
None

## Design Decisions
Added per commit during implementation, as in #53 and #54.

## Scope
medium (3 points). Touches two parts of the pull request page, the merge box and the sidebar's dependency lists, plus one new message; moderate changes to the page's data and templates, with browser tests for both parts.

## AI Disclosure
Used claude-code for the drafting of this issue, followed by my changes and proofing. Changes after the spec review were also made with claude-code.

        Course rules win where they differ from upstream: PRs here are merged with a merge commit, and AI logs and .claude-students docs are committed on purpose.
        - Scope: a PR covers one issue. Flag changes unrelated to the linked issue (CONTRIBUTING.md: "Don't make changes unrelated to your PR").
        - Layers: imports flow cmd → routers → services → models → modules only. Flag an import against that direction.
        - Comments: short, explaining why, never narrating the code. Flag a removed comment that is still true. Never ask for docstrings.

If possible, the message also names the person who approved the change, since a human approves every commit.

    - path: "**/*.go"
      instructions: |
        - A new .go file starts with `// Copyright <current year> The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.` and `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`.
        - Writes that must roll back together run inside `db.WithTx` or `db.WithTx2`, and every function in the transaction takes `context.Context` first.
        - XORM: flag an `Update` or `Delete` with no `Where` or ID condition; it touches every row.
        - Before reading or changing another user's or repository's data, the doer's permission is checked. Treat a missing check as a security bug.
        - Handlers fail through the context helpers (`ctx.NotFound`, `ctx.ServerError`, `ctx.JSONError` and the like), never by writing the response by hand.
        - User-visible text is a locale key, never a literal; user-facing errors go through `util.ErrorWrapTranslatable`.
        - `go.mod` and `go.sum` change only when the feature needs it, after `make tidy`.
    - path: "**/*_test.go"
      instructions: |
        - Prefer a unit test next to the code over an integration test when the logic can be tested alone (AGENTS.md).
        - A new test package has `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }`, or its fixtures never load.
        - Cover the normal case, invalid input and permission checks where they apply (docs/sprint0/standards.md).
        - Integration tests should run in under 2 seconds. Don't ask for tests beyond what the acceptance criteria need.
    - path: "models/migrations/**"

        - It lives in `v1_27/v<id>.go` and declares its own local copy of each struct inside the function. It never imports a live model from `models/`.
        - Partial table changes use `SyncWithOptions` with `IgnoreDropIndices` and `IgnoreConstrains`, not plain `Sync`.
        - A column added to an existing table is `NOT NULL DEFAULT <value>`, so old rows are filled.

        - Status codes: GET 200, POST 201 with the created object, PUT 204, PATCH 200 with the changed object, DELETE 204.
        - Edit endpoints take every field as optional except the ones that identify the object. List endpoints accept `page` and `limit` and set `X-Total-Count` via `ctx.SetTotalCountHeader`.

    - path: "modules/structs/**"

    - path: "templates/**"

    - path: "web_src/js/**"

        - Use `!` rather than `?.` or `??` when a value always exists (AGENTS.md).
        - Mark a function `async` only when it awaits or returns a Promise. An async event listener calls `e.preventDefault()` before its first `await`.
        - Requests use the `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` wrappers from `modules/fetch.ts`. Read data attributes with `getAttribute`, not `dataset`, and never bind user-provided data directly onto DOM nodes.

        - Don't mix Vue with Fomantic-UI, and don't use JSX.

    - path: "web_src/css/**"

Each acceptance criterion of the linked issue has a row (for a bug report, the Expected Behavior); a PR that changes no product behaviour may write "N/A" with a reason.           - "AI assistance" either says "No AI used", or names the tool and model, what the AI did, and what the author did to check it.

      - name: Tests for behaviour changes

          Otherwise pass only if at least one test file was added or changed: a *_test.go file, a *.test.ts file, or a file under tests/. On fail, list the changed code files.

5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status. If CI doesn't run your tests, the commands you ran and
   a summary of the results (passed, failed, skipped).
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>

   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6; tests written or updated
appropriately, with the Test Evidence section complete, every AC covered and expected values
justified 6; description explains what and why, Tech Debt section present, issue linked 3; CI passes
or manual verification documented 3; reviewed with the rubric (including the test evidence row),
reviewer comment posted, merged only after an approval on the latest commit 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything

<!-- Rules are numbered continuously 1-15 across the sections below; check.sh error
     messages and all 34 docs cite them by number, so the sequence must not restart. -->

# Maintenance rules

Five people maintain one shared set of docs. These rules exist so the set stays *one* set. Read
them before editing anything in `.claude-students/`. Rules marked **[checked]** are enforced by
`./.claude-students/check.sh`.

## Scope discipline

1. **Upstream wins.** `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/guidelines-*.md` are authoritative.
   Docs here summarise them and link to them; they never restate a rule differently and never
   contradict one. A contradiction is a bug in this folder, not in the project.
2. **One fact, one home.** Every fact lives in exactly one doc — the one whose `scope:` owns that
   path. Everywhere else, link to it. Duplicated facts are how five maintainers end up with five
   different answers.
3. **Durability test.** Record a fact only if it (a) took more than one discovery step to find and
   (b) will still be true after the next upstream merge. A one-off workaround, a sprint detail or
   anything about your own task fails this test — that belongs in `ai-logs/`.
4. **No process notes.** No TODOs, no open questions, no first person, no student names, no dates
   other than `verified-at`. This is a map of the code, not a journal.

## Form

5. **Template only [checked].** Use the `## ` headings from `_TEMPLATE.md`, all of them, in that
   order, with nothing added. If a section has nothing to say, write one line saying so.
6. **120-line cap [checked].** Going over means the scope is too broad. Split the doc, and add the
   new `INDEX.md` row in the same commit. `INDEX.md` itself is capped at 60 lines.
7. **Cite or delete [checked, partially].** Every claim names a repo path. A claim with no path is
   unverifiable by the next reader — delete it.
8. **Symbols, not line numbers [checked].** Write `models/db/context.go` → `WithTx`, never
   `models/db/context.go:143`. Line numbers rot at the next upstream merge and a stale number is
   worse than no number. Code fences stay at 10 lines or fewer — point at the file instead of
   copying it.
9. **Repo-relative paths [checked].** `models/db/context.go`, never `/home/you/gitea/models/...`.
10. **Whitespace [checked].** No trailing whitespace, LF endings, final newline — same as the rest
    of the repo (`.editorconfig`).

## Change control

11. **One universal set.** These docs live on `main` and nowhere else. Never keep a personal copy,
    a per-student folder, or a long-lived branch of them.
12. **Changes land by PR**, titled `docs(context): <subject>` per `AGENTS.md` Conventional Commits,
    with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer and no `Co-Authored-By` or
    `Signed-off-by`.
13. **Fix in place.** If you discover while working that a doc is wrong or incomplete, correct it
    in the *same* PR as your code change and update `verified-at` to the commit you checked
    against. Leaving a doc stale for someone else to hit is the exact failure this folder exists to
    prevent. This rule applies to AI sessions too.
14. **New docs need three things in one commit [checked]:** the file, its `INDEX.md` row, and a
    `scope:` that does not overlap any existing doc's. If the scope overlaps, you wanted to edit
    that doc, not add one.
15. **`./.claude-students/check.sh` passes before you push [checked].** It is dependency-free and
    finishes in under a second.

## The guide layer (rules 16-22)

`guide/` holds a plain-English page for each reference page in `docs/`, same filename. It exists so
a person new to Go and to this codebase can get oriented. It is **derived**, not independent.

16. Every guide carries `source:`, `source-hash:` and `verified-at:` in its frontmatter **[checked]**.
17. A guide's `source:` names a real `docs/*.md` with the **same filename** **[checked]**.
18. `source-hash:` is the first 16 characters of `sha256sum docs/<name>.md`. If the reference page
    changes and the guide is not regenerated, `check.sh` reports **drift** **[checked]**. Regenerating
    means: reread the reference page, rewrite the guide, update the hash and `verified-at`.
19. Guide headings match `guide/_TEMPLATE.md` exactly and in order **[checked]**.
20. Guides are capped at **200 lines**, code fences at **30** **[checked]** — teaching needs more room
    than reference does.
21. **A guide adds explanation, vocabulary and worked steps. It adds no new facts.** Every repo path
    a guide cites must also be cited by its source page **[checked]**. If you need a fact the
    reference page lacks, add it *there* first, which bumps the hash and forces the guide to be
    regenerated in the same commit — exactly the intended order.
22. `guide/START-HERE.md` has no source page. It is exempt from rules 17, 18 and 21, and is where
    cross-cutting material lives that no single reference page owns.

**Never fix a fact in `guide/`.** If the two layers disagree, the reference page is the truth and
the guide is stale: fix `docs/`, regenerate the guide, ship both in one PR. A disagreement is a bug
report against `docs/`, not an editing job in `guide/`.

**Known limitation:** a hand-edit to a guide that only rewords prose is not mechanically
detectable. Rule 21 catches invented facts; rule 18 catches a stale guide; review catches the rest.

## Updating `verified-at`

`verified-at` is the short SHA the doc was last checked against, from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
Bump it whenever you confirm or correct a doc. A doc whose `verified-at` is far behind `main` has
not been checked recently — treat its details as hints and confirm them in the code before relying
on them.

+
+// GetMergeBlockingDependencies returns the dependencies that block merging pr, each with its repository loaded.
+func GetMergeBlockingDependencies(ctx context.Context, pr *PullRequest) (issueDeps []*DependencyInfo, err error) {
+	err = db.GetEngine(ctx).
+		Table("issue").
+		Join("INNER", "repository", "repository.id = issue.repo_id").
+		Join("INNER", "issue_dependency", "issue_dependency.dependency_id = issue.id").
+		Where("issue_dependency.issue_id = ?", pr.IssueID).
+		And(mergeBlockingDependencyCond()).
+		Find(&issueDeps)
+
+	for _, depInfo := range issueDeps {
+		depInfo.Issue.Repo = &depInfo.Repository
+	}
+
+	return issueDeps, err
+}
+
+// mergeBlockingDependencyCond matches an open issue or pull request, or a pull request closed without merging.
+// Shared so the merge check and the merge box list the same dependencies.
+func mergeBlockingDependencyCond() builder.Cond {
+	return builder.Or(
+		builder.Eq{"issue.is_closed": false},
+		builder.In("issue.id", builder.Select("issue_id").From("pull_request").Where(builder.Eq{"has_merged": false})),
+	)
+}

+		ctx.ServerError("LoadPullRequests", err)
+		return
+	}
 
+	ctx.Data["BlockedByDependencies"], ctx.Data["BlockedByDependenciesNotPermitted"] = checkBlockedByIssues(ctx, blockedBy)
+	if ctx.Written() {
+		return
+	}
 	ctx.Data["BlockingDependencies"], ctx.Data["BlockingDependenciesNotPermitted"] = checkBlockedByIssues(ctx, blocking)
 }
 
+// loadDependencyPullRequests loads the pull request of each dependency that is one, so the sidebar can tell merged from closed
+func loadDependencyPullRequests(ctx *context.Context, depLists ...[]*issues_model.DependencyInfo) error {
+	var issues issues_model.IssueList
+	for _, deps := range depLists {
+		for _, dep := range deps {
+			issues = append(issues, &dep.Issue)
+		}
+	}
+	return issues.LoadPullRequests(ctx)
+}

+// prepareMergeBoxDependencies lists the dependencies that block merging, the same ones the merge check refuses.
+func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) prepareMergeBoxDependencies(ctx *context.Context) {
+	if !ctx.Repo.Repository.IsDependenciesEnabled(ctx) {
+		return
+	}
+	deps, err := issues_model.GetMergeBlockingDependencies(ctx, prInfo.issue.PullRequest)
+	if err != nil {
+		ctx.ServerError("GetMergeBlockingDependencies", err)
+		return
+	}
+	if len(deps) == 0 {
+		return
+	}
+	prInfo.MergeBoxData.isBlockedByDependencies = true
+	canRead, notPermitted := checkBlockedByIssues(ctx, deps)
+	if ctx.Written() {
+		return
+	}
+
+	items := make([]template.HTML, 0, len(canRead)+1)
+	for _, dep := range canRead {
+		// as the timeline shows a dependency: the repository only when it is another one
+		if dep.Issue.RepoID == prInfo.issue.RepoID {
+			items = append(items, htmlutil.HTMLFormat(`<a href="%s">#%d %s</a>`, dep.Issue.Link(), dep.Issue.Index, dep.Issue.Title))
+		} else {
+			items = append(items, htmlutil.HTMLFormat(`<a href="%s">%s#%d - %s</a>`, dep.Issue.Link(), dep.Issue.Repo.FullName(), dep.Issue.Index, dep.Issue.Title))
+		}
+	}
+	if len(notPermitted) > 0 {
+		items = append(items, ctx.Locale.TrN(len(notPermitted), "repo.issues.dependency.no_permission_1", "repo.issues.dependency.no_permission_n", len(notPermitted)))
+	}
+	prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddErrorItem(ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.blocked_by_dependencies"), items)
+}

+{{/* A dependency's state in the sidebar: Merged for a merged pull request, otherwise Open or Closed. Needs its PullRequest loaded. */}}
+{{- if and .IsPull .PullRequest .PullRequest.HasMerged -}}
+	{{- ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.pulls.merged" -}}
+{{- else if .IsClosed -}}
+	{{- ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.issues.closed_title" -}}
+{{- else -}}
+	{{- ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.issues.open_title" -}}
+{{- end -}}

+func TestGetMergeBlockingDependencies(t *testing.T) {
+	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
+	doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 1})
+	pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2}) // issue 3, repo 1
+	require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
+
+	// one dependency of each kind in the issue's table, closed first where needed
+	for _, dep := range []struct {
+		issueID int64
+		close   bool
+	}{
+		{1, false},  // open issue
+		{5, false},  // closed issue, closed in the fixtures
+		{2, true},   // merged pull request 1; closed as a real merge would, the fixture leaves it open
+		{11, true},  // pull request 5, closed without merging
+		{12, false}, // open pull request 6, in repo 3
+	} {
+		issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: dep.issueID})
+		if dep.close {
+			_, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer, issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{})
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+		}
+		require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(t.Context(), doer, pr.Issue, issue))
+	}
+
+	deps, err := issues_model.GetMergeBlockingDependencies(t.Context(), pr)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	repoByIssue := map[int64]int64{}
+	for _, dep := range deps {
+		require.NotNil(t, dep.Issue.Repo, "issue %d has no repository loaded", dep.Issue.ID)
+		repoByIssue[dep.Issue.ID] = dep.Issue.Repo.ID // the merge box links each dependency to its own repository
+	}
+	assert.Equal(t, map[int64]int64{1: 1, 11: 1, 12: 3}, repoByIssue)
+}

+
+func TestIssueViewSidebarDependencyStates(t *testing.T) {
+	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
+	translation.InitLocales(t.Context()) // the expected texts are the English ones
+	owner := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
+	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
+	issuesUnit, err := repo.GetUnit(t.Context(), unit.TypeIssues)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	issuesUnit.IssuesConfig().EnableDependencies = true // fixture repos leave it unset, which reads as off
+	require.NoError(t, repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig(t.Context(), issuesUnit))
+
+	// in user2/repo1: issue 1 (#1) open, issue 2 (#2) merged pull request 1, issue 3 (#3) open pull request 2,
+	// issue 5 (#4) closed in the fixtures, issue 11 (#5) pull request 5 closed without merging; issue 7 is #2 in the private user2/repo2
+	for _, id := range []int64{2, 11} { // pull request 1 is merged but the fixture leaves it open, so close it as a real merge would
+		_, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: id}), owner, issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{})
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+	}
+	for _, dep := range [][2]int64{{3, 1}, {3, 2}, {3, 5}, {3, 11}, {3, 7}, {2, 1}, {5, 1}, {11, 1}} { // {issue, the issue it depends on}
+		issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: dep[0]})
+		require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(t.Context(), owner, issue, unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: dep[1]})))
+	}
+
+	// the entries of one sidebar list ("Depends on" or "Blocks") on issueID's page, as viewerID reads them
+	sidebarList := func(t *testing.T, viewerID, issueID int64, heading string) []string {
+		ctx, resp := contexttest.MockContext(t, "/", contexttest.MockContextOption{Render: templates.PageRenderer()})
+		ctx.Locale = translation.NewLocale("en-US")
+		ctx.TemplateContext["Locale"] = ctx.Locale // templates read the locale the context was created with
+		contexttest.LoadUser(t, ctx, viewerID)
+		contexttest.LoadRepo(t, ctx, 1)
+		issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: issueID})
+		require.NoError(t, issue.LoadRepo(ctx))
+		ctx.Data["Issue"] = issue
+		ctx.Data["Repository"] = ctx.Repo.Repository
+
+		prepareIssueViewSidebarDependency(ctx, issue)
+		require.False(t, ctx.Written())
+		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, "repo/issue/sidebar/issue_dependencies")
+
+		doc, err := goquery.NewDocumentFromReader(resp.Body)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		entries := []string{}
+		doc.Find("strong").FilterFunction(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) bool { return s.Text() == heading }).
+			Parent().Next().Find(".item").Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
+			// tests render each icon as its name in a span; AC5 asks for the state word, so leave the icons out
+			s.Find("span").FilterFunction(func(_ int, e *goquery.Selection) bool {
+				return e.Children().Length() == 0 && strings.HasPrefix(e.Text(), "octicon-")
+			}).Remove()
+			entries = append(entries, strings.Join(strings.Fields(s.Text()), " "))
+		})
+		return entries
+	}
+
+	t.Run("AC5 Depends on", func(t *testing.T) {
+		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
+			"#1 issue1 user2/repo1 · Open",
+			"#2 issue2 user2/repo1 · Merged",
+			"#4 issue5 user2/repo1 · Closed",
+			"#5 pull5 user2/repo1 · Closed",
+			"#2 issue7 user2/repo2 · Open",
+		}, sidebarList(t, 2, 3, "Depends on"))
+	})
+	t.Run("AC5 Blocks", func(t *testing.T) {
+		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
+			"#3 issue3 user2/repo1 · Open",
+			"#2 issue2 user2/repo1 · Merged",
+			"#4 issue5 user2/repo1 · Closed",
+			"#5 pull5 user2/repo1 · Closed",
+		}, sidebarList(t, 2, 1, "Blocks"))
+	})
+	t.Run("AC5 an entry the viewer can remove but not read", func(t *testing.T) {
+		// user40 may write to user2/repo1, so it manages dependencies, but cannot read user2/repo2
+		assert.Contains(t, sidebarList(t, 40, 3, "Depends on"), "#2 issue7 user2/repo2 · Open")
+	})
+}

+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package repo
+
+import (
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
+	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
+	"gitea.dev/models/unit"

+	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/translation"

+
+	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+// mockPullWithDependencies opens pull request 2 (issue 3 in user2/repo1) as viewerID, after user2 gives it the dependencies depIDs.
+// It loads the real English locale, as the expected texts are the English ones.
+func mockPullWithDependencies(t *testing.T, viewerID int64, dependenciesEnabled bool, depIDs ...int64) (*context.Context, *pullRequestViewInfo) {
+	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
+	translation.InitLocales(t.Context())
+	owner := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
+	pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2})
+	require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
+	for _, depID := range depIDs {
+		dep := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: depID})
+		require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(t.Context(), owner, pr.Issue, dep))
+	}
+	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
+	issuesUnit, err := repo.GetUnit(t.Context(), unit.TypeIssues)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	issuesUnit.IssuesConfig().EnableDependencies = dependenciesEnabled // fixture repos leave it unset, which reads as off
+	require.NoError(t, repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig(t.Context(), issuesUnit))
+
+	ctx, _ := contexttest.MockContext(t, "user2/repo1/pulls/2")
+	ctx.Locale = translation.NewLocale("en-US")
+	contexttest.LoadUser(t, ctx, viewerID)
+	contexttest.LoadRepo(t, ctx, 1)
+	return ctx, &pullRequestViewInfo{issue: pr.Issue, MergeBoxData: &pullMergeBoxData{}}
+}
+
+func TestPrepareMergeBoxDependencies(t *testing.T) {
+	// the merge box's blockers as text: each message, then each of its list entries as "text -> link"
+	blockers := func(t *testing.T, viewerID int64, dependenciesEnabled bool, depIDs ...int64) []string {
+		ctx, prInfo := mockPullWithDependencies(t, viewerID, dependenciesEnabled, depIDs...)
+		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxDependencies(ctx)
+		require.False(t, ctx.Written())
+
+		texts := []string{}
+		for _, item := range prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.items {
+			texts = append(texts, string(item.InfoHTML))
+			for _, listItem := range item.ListItems {
+				doc, err := goquery.NewDocumentFromReader(strings.NewReader(string(listItem)))
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				text := strings.TrimSpace(doc.Text())
+				if href, ok := doc.Find("a").Attr("href"); ok {
+					text += " -> " + href
+				}
+				texts = append(texts, text)
+			}
+		}
+		return texts
+	}
+
+	t.Run("AC1 links each blocking dependency", func(t *testing.T) {
+		// issue 1 (#1) is in the same repository, issue 7 (#2) in user2/repo2
+		texts := blockers(t, 2, true, 1, 7)
+		require.NotEmpty(t, texts)
+		assert.Equal(t, "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:", texts[0])
+		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
+			"#1 issue1 -> /user2/repo1/issues/1",
+			"user2/repo2#2 - issue7 -> /user2/repo2/issues/2",
+		}, texts[1:])
+	})
+	t.Run("AC3 no dependencies", func(t *testing.T) {
+		assert.Empty(t, blockers(t, 2, true))
+	})
+	t.Run("AC4 counts a dependency the viewer cannot read", func(t *testing.T) {
+		// user4 can read the public user2/repo1 but not the private user2/repo2
+		texts := blockers(t, 4, true, 1, 7)
+		require.NotEmpty(t, texts)
+		assert.Equal(t, "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:", texts[0])
+		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
+			"#1 issue1 -> /user2/repo1/issues/1",
+			"You do not have permission to read 1 dependency",
+		}, texts[1:])
+	})
+	t.Run("AC6 dependencies turned off", func(t *testing.T) {
+		assert.Empty(t, blockers(t, 2, false, 1, 7))
+	})
+}
+
+func TestPrepareMergeBoxFormWithDependencies(t *testing.T) {
+	type offer struct {
+		styles   []string // the merge styles offered, "+auto" where "(When checks succeed)" is offered with it; nil when there is no merge form
+		messages []string
+	}
+	// user2 owns user2/repo1 and may merge pull request 2, whose branch merges cleanly. checksPending holds the merge back
+	// for status checks user2 cannot bypass, which is when "(When checks succeed)" is offered.
+	mergeBox := func(t *testing.T, allowManualMerge, checksPending bool, depIDs ...int64) offer {
+		ctx, prInfo := mockPullWithDependencies(t, 2, true, depIDs...)
+		contexttest.LoadGitRepo(t, ctx)
+		defer ctx.Repo.GitRepo.Close()
+		ctx.Repo.Repository.MustGetUnit(ctx, unit.TypePullRequests).PullRequestsConfig().AllowManualMerge = allowManualMerge
+		data := prInfo.MergeBoxData
+		data.hasPermToMerge = true
+		data.hasOverridableBlockers = checksPending
+		data.canMergeNow = !checksPending
+
+		// in the order prepareMergeBox runs them
+		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxDependencies(ctx)
+		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxFormProps(ctx)
+		prInfo.prepareMergeBoxInfoItems(ctx)
+		require.False(t, ctx.Written())
+
+		var o offer
+		if data.MergeFormProps != nil {
+			for _, s := range data.MergeFormProps["mergeStyles"].([]any) {
+				style := s.(map[string]any)
+				if !style["allowed"].(bool) {
+					continue
+				}
+				name := style["name"].(string)
+				if !style["hideAutoMerge"].(bool) {
+					name += "+auto"
+				}
+				o.styles = append(o.styles, name)
+			}
+		}
+		for _, section := range data.InfoSections {
+			for _, item := range section.InfoItems {
+				o.messages = append(o.messages, string(item.InfoHTML))
+			}
+		}
+		return o
+	}
+
+	t.Run("AC2 only Manually merged while blocked", func(t *testing.T) {
+		o := mergeBox(t, true, false, 1)
+		assert.Equal(t, []string{"manually-merged"}, o.styles)
+		assert.NotContains(t, o.messages, "This pull request can be merged automatically.")
+	})
+	t.Run("AC2 no merge form while blocked and waiting for checks", func(t *testing.T) {
+		o := mergeBox(t, false, true, 1)
+		assert.Nil(t, o.styles)
+		assert.NotContains(t, o.messages, "This pull request cannot be merged because all repository merge options are disabled.")
+	})
+	t.Run("control: waiting for checks offers (When checks succeed)", func(t *testing.T) {
+		assert.Contains(t, mergeBox(t, false, true).styles, "merge+auto")
+	})
+	t.Run("AC3 resolved dependencies look as with none", func(t *testing.T) {
+		none := mergeBox(t, false, false)
+		// the styles user2/repo1 allows: four in its fixture, plus fast-forward-only, which is on by default
+		assert.Equal(t, []string{"merge", "rebase", "rebase-merge", "squash", "fast-forward-only"}, none.styles)
+		assert.Contains(t, none.messages, "This pull request can be merged automatically.")
+		assert.Equal(t, none, mergeBox(t, false, false, 5)) // issue 5 is closed
+	})
+}

+import {env} from 'node:process';
+import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
+import type {APIRequestContext} from '@playwright/test';
+import {apiCreateFile, apiCreateIssue, apiCreatePR, apiCreateRepo, apiEditRepo, apiHeaders, baseUrl, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';
+
+const owner = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;
+
+// a repository whose issues can have dependencies, set here rather than left to the server's default
+async function createRepoWithDependencies(request: APIRequestContext, name: string, extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}) {
+  await apiCreateRepo(request, {name});
+  await apiEditRepo(request, owner, name, {
+    has_issues: true, // the API ignores internal_tracker without it
+    internal_tracker: {enable_time_tracker: true, allow_only_contributors_to_track_time: true, enable_issue_dependencies: true},
+    ...extra,
+  });
+}
+
+async function createPull(request: APIRequestContext, repo: string, branch: string, title: string) {
+  await apiCreateFile(request, owner, repo, `${branch}.txt`, `${branch}\n`, {newBranch: branch});
+  return apiCreatePR(request, owner, repo, branch, 'main', title);
+}
+
+async function addDependency(request: APIRequestContext, repo: string, index: number, dependsOn: number) {
+  const response = await request.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${index}/dependencies`, {
+    headers: apiHeaders(),
+    data: {owner, repo, index: dependsOn},
+  });
+  expect(response.ok()).toBeTruthy();
+}
+
+test('#144 AC1 AC2 the merge box names the blocking dependency and offers only Manually merged', async ({page, request}) => {
+  const repo = `e2e-merge-deps-${randomString(8)}`;
+  await createRepoWithDependencies(request, repo, {allow_manual_merge: true});
+  const pull = await createPull(request, repo, 'blocked', 'Blocked pull');
+  const {index: issue} = await apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo, title: 'Open dependency'});
+  await Promise.all([addDependency(request, repo, pull, issue), login(page)]);
+
+  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repo}/pulls/${pull}`);
+  const mergeBox = page.locator('.pull-merge-box');
+  await expect(mergeBox.getByText('This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:')).toBeVisible();
+  await expect(mergeBox.getByRole('link', {name: `#${issue} Open dependency`})).toHaveAttribute('href', `/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${issue}`);
+
+  // wait for the merge form to load before checking what it offers, so an empty form cannot pass
+  await expect(mergeBox.getByRole('button', {name: 'Manually merged'})).toBeVisible();
+  await mergeBox.locator('.merge-button .dropdown').click();
+  await expect(mergeBox.locator('.merge-button .menu .item')).toHaveText(['Manually merged']); // no other style, no "(When checks succeed)"
+});
+
+test('#144 AC5 the sidebar shows each dependency as Open, Closed or Merged', async ({page, request}) => {
+  const repo = `e2e-dep-states-${randomString(8)}`;
+  await createRepoWithDependencies(request, repo);
+  const {index: subject} = await apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo, title: 'Subject'});
+  const [{index: open}, closed, merged] = await Promise.all([
+    apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo, title: 'Open issue'}),
+    createPull(request, repo, 'closed', 'Closed pull'),
+    createPull(request, repo, 'merged', 'Merged pull'),
+  ]);
+  const pulls = `${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/pulls`;
+  expect((await request.patch(`${pulls}/${closed}`, {headers: apiHeaders(), data: {state: 'closed'}})).ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  await expect(async () => { // the merge is refused until the new pull request's conflict check has finished
+    expect((await request.post(`${pulls}/${merged}/merge`, {headers: apiHeaders(), data: {Do: 'merge'}})).ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  }).toPass();
+  await Promise.all([
+    ...[open, closed, merged].map((dep) => addDependency(request, repo, subject, dep)),
+    login(page),
+  ]);
+
+  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${subject}`);
+  const entries = page.locator('.ui.depending .item.dependency');
+  await expect(entries.filter({hasText: `#${open} Open issue`})).toContainText('· Open');
+  await expect(entries.filter({hasText: `#${closed} Closed pull`})).toContainText('· Closed');
+  await expect(entries.filter({hasText: `#${merged} Merged pull`})).toContainText('· Merged');
+});

	if hasPendingPullRequestMerge {

	defaultSquashMergeTitle, defaultSquashMergeBody, err := pull_service.GetDefaultMergeMessage(ctx, ctx.Repo.GitRepo, pull, repo_model.MergeStyleSquash)

	if !prInfo.IsPullRequestBroken {

	// if this pr can be merged now, then hide the auto merge
	generalHideAutoMerge := prInfo.MergeBoxData.canMergeNow && allOverridableChecksOk

	// dependencies leave only "Manually merged", which the merge check does not hold back
	canUseMergeStyles := pull.IsStatusMergeable() && !prInfo.MergeBoxData.isBlockedByDependencies

				"textDoMerge":           ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.merge_pull_request"),
				"mergeTitleFieldText":   defaultMergeTitle,
				"mergeMessageFieldText": defaultMergeBody,
				"hideAutoMerge":         generalHideAutoMerge,
			},

				"hideMergeMessageTexts": true,
				"hideAutoMerge":         generalHideAutoMerge,

			map[string]any{

				"hideAutoMerge":         generalHideAutoMerge,

			map[string]any{

				"mergeTitleFieldText":   defaultSquashMergeTitle,
				"mergeMessageFieldText": defaultSquashMergeCommitMessages + defaultSquashMergeBody,
				"hideAutoMerge":         generalHideAutoMerge,
			},
			map[string]any{
				"name":                  "fast-forward-only",
				"allowed":               prConfig.AllowFastForwardOnly && pull.CommitsBehind == 0,
				"textDoMerge":           ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.fast_forward_only_merge_pull_request"),
				"hideMergeMessageTexts": true,
				"hideAutoMerge":         generalHideAutoMerge,
			},
		}
	}

	// Manually Merged is not a well-known feature, it is used to mark a non-mergeable PR (already merged, conflicted) as merged
	// To test it:
	//  Enable "Manually Merged" feature in the Repository Settings
	//  Create a pull request, either:
	//  - Merge the pull request branch locally and push the merged commit to Gitea
	//  - Make some conflicts between the base branch and the pull request branch
	//  Then the Manually Merged form will be shown in the merge form
	canUseManualMerge := !pull.IsWorkInProgress(ctx) && !pull.IsChecking() && prConfig.AllowManualMerge
	if canUseManualMerge {
		mergeStyles = append(mergeStyles, map[string]any{
			"name":                  "manually-merged",
			"allowed":               prConfig.AllowManualMerge,
			"textDoMerge":           ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.merge_manually"),
			"hideMergeMessageTexts": true,
			"hideAutoMerge":         true,
		})
	}

	if len(mergeStyles) > 0 {
		mergeFormProps["mergeStyles"] = mergeStyles
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.MergeFormProps = mergeFormProps
	} else if canUseMergeStyles {
		// no merge style was set in repo setting
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
			svg.RenderHTML("octicon-x", 16, "tw-text-red"),
			ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.no_merge_desc"),

		prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
			svg.RenderHTML("octicon-info"),
			ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.no_merge_helper"),
		)
	}

	deps, err := issues_model.GetMergeBlockingDependencies(ctx, prInfo.issue.PullRequest)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetMergeBlockingDependencies", err)
		return
	}
	if len(deps) == 0 {
		return
	}
	prInfo.MergeBoxData.isBlockedByDependencies = true
	canRead, notPermitted := checkBlockedByIssues(ctx, deps)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}

	items := make([]template.HTML, 0, len(canRead)+1)
	for _, dep := range canRead {
		// as the timeline shows a dependency: the repository only when it is another one
		if dep.Issue.RepoID == prInfo.issue.RepoID {
			items = append(items, htmlutil.HTMLFormat(`<a href="%s">#%d %s</a>`, dep.Issue.Link(), dep.Issue.Index, dep.Issue.Title))
		} else {
			items = append(items, htmlutil.HTMLFormat(`<a href="%s">%s#%d - %s</a>`, dep.Issue.Link(), dep.Issue.Repo.FullName(), dep.Issue.Index, dep.Issue.Title))
		}
	}
	if len(notPermitted) > 0 {
		items = append(items, ctx.Locale.TrN(len(notPermitted), "repo.issues.dependency.no_permission_1", "repo.issues.dependency.no_permission_n", len(notPermitted)))
	}
	prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddErrorItem(ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.blocked_by_dependencies"), items)
}

func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) prepareMergeBoxInfoItems(ctx *context.Context) {
	pull := prInfo.issue.PullRequest
	data := prInfo.MergeBoxData

	if pull.HasMerged && data.IsPullBranchDeletable {
		data.ClosedInfoTitle = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.merged_success")
		data.ClosedInfoBody = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.merged_info_text", htmlutil.HTMLFormat("<code>%s</code>", prInfo.headTarget))
		return
	} else if prInfo.issue.IsClosed {
		data.ClosedInfoTitle = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.closed")
		if prInfo.IsPullRequestBroken {
			data.ClosedInfoBody = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.cant_reopen_deleted_branch")
		} else {
			data.ClosedInfoBody = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.reopen_to_merge")
		}
		return
	}

	if pull.IsFilesConflicted() {
		detailItems := escapeStringSliceToHTML(pull.ConflictedFiles)
		if len(detailItems) == 0 {
			detailItems = append(detailItems, ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.files_conflicted_no_listed_files"))
		}
		if len(detailItems) > 10 {
			detailItems = detailItems[:10]
			detailItems = append(detailItems, "...")
		}
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
			svg.RenderHTML("octicon-x"),
			ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.files_conflicted"),
			detailItems,
		)
	}

	if prInfo.IsPullRequestBroken {
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
			svg.RenderHTML("octicon-x"),
			ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.data_broken"),
		)
	}

	if pull.IsChecking() {
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
			svg.RenderHTML("gitea-running", 16, "rotate-clockwise"),
			ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.is_checking"),
		)
	}

	if pull.IsAncestor() {
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
			svg.RenderHTML("octicon-alert"),
			ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.is_ancestor"),
		)
	}

	if !pull.IsStatusMergeable() {
		// it is only a "protection" level blocker, it can be bypassed by admin (e.g.: manually merged)
		if pull.IsEmpty() {
			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddInfoItem(
				svg.RenderHTML("octicon-alert"),
				ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.is_empty"),
			)
		} else {
			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddErrorItem(ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.cannot_auto_merge_desc"))
			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddInfoItem(
				svg.RenderHTML("octicon-info"),
				ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.cannot_auto_merge_helper"),
			)
		}
	}

	if !data.hasPermToMerge {
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddInfoItem(
			svg.RenderHTML("octicon-info"),
			ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.no_merge_access"),
		)
	}

	if data.canMergeNow && !data.isBlockedByDependencies {
		if data.hasOverridableBlockers {
			prompt := ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.required_status_check_bypass_allowlist")
			if data.canBypassProtectionAsAdmin {
				prompt = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.required_status_check_administrator")
			}
			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoMergePrompts.AddInfoItem(
				svg.RenderHTML("octicon-dot-fill"),
				prompt,
			)
		} else if pull.IsStatusMergeable() || pull.IsEmpty() {
			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoMergePrompts.AddInfoItem(
				svg.RenderHTML("octicon-check"),
				ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.can_auto_merge_desc"),
			)
		}
	}

	if len(data.infoCommitBlockers.items) > 0 {
		data.InfoSections = append(data.InfoSections, &pullInfoSection{data.infoCommitBlockers.items})
	} else {
		data.InfoSections = append(data.InfoSections, &pullInfoSection{data.infoProtectionBlockers.items})
	}
	data.InfoSections = append(data.InfoSections, &pullInfoSection{data.infoMergePrompts.items})
}

const mergeStyleAllowedCount = shallowRef(0);

const showMergeStyleMenu = shallowRef(false);
const showActionForm = shallowRef(false);

const mergeButtonStyleClass = computed(() => {
  if (mergeStyle.value === mergeStyleManuallyMerged) return 'red';
  if (mergeForm.allOverridableChecksOk) return 'primary';
  return autoMergeWhenSucceed.value ? 'primary' : 'red';
});

const mergeSelectStyleClass = computed(() => {
  if (mergeForm.emptyCommit) return '';
  if (mergeStyle.value === mergeStyleManuallyMerged) return 'red';
  return 'primary';
});

const forceMerge = computed(() => {
  return mergeForm.canMergeNow && !mergeForm.allOverridableChecksOk;
});

watch(mergeStyle, (val) => {
  mergeStyleDetail.value = mergeForm.mergeStyles.find((e: any) => e.name === val);
  for (const elem of document.querySelectorAll('[data-pull-merge-style]')) {
    toggleElem(elem, elem.getAttribute('data-pull-merge-style') === val);
  }
});

onMounted(() => {
  mergeStyleAllowedCount.value = mergeForm.mergeStyles.reduce((v: any, msd: any) => v + (msd.allowed ? 1 : 0), 0);

  let mergeStyle = mergeForm.mergeStyles.find((e: any) => e.allowed && e.name === mergeForm.defaultMergeStyle)?.name;
  if (!mergeStyle) mergeStyle = mergeForm.mergeStyles.find((e: any) => e.allowed)?.name;
  switchMergeStyle(mergeStyle, !mergeForm.canMergeNow);

  document.addEventListener('mouseup', hideMergeStyleMenu);
});

onUnmounted(() => {
  document.removeEventListener('mouseup', hideMergeStyleMenu);
});

function hideMergeStyleMenu() {
  showMergeStyleMenu.value = false;
}

function toggleActionForm(show: boolean) {
  showActionForm.value = show;
  if (!show) return;
  deleteBranchAfterMerge.value = mergeForm.defaultDeleteBranchAfterMerge;
  mergeTitleFieldValue.value = mergeStyleDetail.value.mergeTitleFieldText;
  mergeMessageFieldValue.value = mergeStyleDetail.value.mergeMessageFieldText;
}

function switchMergeStyle(name: string, autoMerge = false) {
  mergeStyle.value = name;
  autoMergeWhenSucceed.value = autoMerge;
}

function clearMergeMessage() {
  mergeMessageFieldValue.value = mergeForm.defaultMergeMessage;
}
</script>
